title: Lindsay Clancy hires Karen Read attorney for high-stakes double jeopardy fight after murder mistrial
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense team adds Martin Weinberg, the attorney who fought Karen Read's retrial, to argue double jeopardy bars a second trial.
story: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, comments after Plymouth County Superior Court Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial when the jury remained deadlocked, discussing his disappointment with the outcome, his criticism of the prosecution, his belief that the evidence supported an acquittal and what he expects next as the case heads toward a potential retrial.
The Massachusetts mother accused of strangling her three young children to death is bringing in the attorney who fought Karen Read’s retrial as she makes a bid to have her own case thrown out.

Lindsay Clancy, whose closely watched murder trial ended in a reported 11-1 split in favor of finding her not criminally responsible, has added veteran Boston attorney Martin Weinberg to her defense team.

Weinberg entered a limited appearance Tuesday to file and argue a forthcoming motion seeking dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds, according to a Plymouth Superior Court filing obtained by Fox News Digital.
The filing states Weinberg will represent Clancy in connection with the dismissal motion and "related matters."
LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS
Lindsay Clancy sits next to her defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court on August 11, 2026. (Jonathan Wiggs/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
The filing does not say when Weinberg will submit the motion. Clancy’s case is next scheduled to return to court Sept. 29.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL
Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after jurors spent seven days deliberating but said they could not reach a unanimous verdict.
Several jurors later revealed that 11 members of the panel supported finding Clancy not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, while one juror voted to convict.
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON SIGNALS HE'S OPEN TO A DEAL, HOPES DA WILL 'REVISIT' CASE
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington addresses reporters as jurors weigh the case against Lindsay Clancy in the 2023 deaths of her three children. (Joseph Prezioso/ AFP via Getty Images)
Clancy’s longtime defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, signaled immediately after the mistrial that he would fight any attempt to put her on trial again.

The defense is expected to argue that the way the mistrial ended bars prosecutors from taking another shot at the case. Prosecutors can generally retry a defendant after a jury deadlocks, but Clancy’s attorneys are expected to claim that the circumstances surrounding her mistrial make a second trial improper.
KAREN READ’S LAWYER SAYS CLANCY DEFENSE ATTORNEY MAY BE ‘CUT FROM A DIFFERENT CLOTH’ AS DELIBERATIONS DRAG ON
Karen Read outside the Norfolk County Superior Court, Friday, June 13, 2025, in Dedham, Mass. (Richard Beetham for Fox New Digital)
Weinberg mounted a similar fight for Read after her 2024 trial ended without a verdict.

Read’s attorneys said jurors later told them they had unanimously agreed to clear her of second-degree murder and leaving the scene of a deadly crash, despite remaining divided on a manslaughter charge.
PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL

Weinberg argued that Read should not face those two charges again. A judge rejected the request, finding that the jury never formally returned not-guilty verdicts and that Read’s attorneys had agreed to the mistrial.

The battle continued in state and federal court before Read was retried in 2025. She was acquitted of second-degree murder, manslaughter and leaving the scene of a deadly crash but convicted of misdemeanor operating under the influence.
DR PHIL SAYS LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL A 'TEACHABLE MOMENT' ON POSTPARTUM PSYCHOSIS: 'THERE WAS A FAILURE HERE'

Lindsay Clancy looks on as jurors enter the courtroom during Clancy's murder trial at the Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on Sept. 4, 2026. (Greg Derr / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
Clancy is accused of strangling her three children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and 8-month-old Callan, with exercise bands inside the family’s Duxbury home in January 2023.
She then jumped from a second-story window in an apparent suicide attempt, leaving her paralyzed, authorities said.
ACCUSED NC KILLER MOM PLANS INSANITY DEFENSE — AS RETIRED JUDGE SAYS MORE MAY FOLLOW LINDSAY CLANCY STRATEGY

Clancy does not deny killing the children but pleaded not guilty because her attorneys say she was not criminally responsible at the time. Her defense argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was heavily medicated when the children died.
Prosecutors countered that Clancy carefully planned the killings, sending her husband, Patrick Clancy, out of the house before attacking the children.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR WHO BACKED THE DEFENSE ALSO PUBLICLY CHEERED KAREN READ'S ACQUITTAL
Defendant Lindsay Clancy listens during her murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass., on Thursday, July 30, 2026. (CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via AP, Pool)
Clancy remains in custody at Tewksbury Hospital. Prosecutors have not publicly announced whether they intend to retry her.

Sullivan also ordered the identities of the 12 jurors and six alternates who served in Clancy’s trial to remain private indefinitely amid safety concerns and the unauthorized disclosure of jurors’ personal information.
The judge wrote that jurors had been identified without their permission and that at least one juror had asked for the protection to be extended indefinitely.

"Based on the circumstances of this trial and the fact that the case continues to receive daily, divisive attention in Massachusetts and beyond, the Court concludes that there is a real and present ‘risk of [personal] harm to the jurors [and] to the integrity of their service,’" Sullivan wrote in the order obtained by Fox News.

Sullivan also found "a risk of immediate and irreparable injury" if the juror list were made public. The order does not prevent jurors from identifying themselves or speaking with the media if they choose.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In a separate order, Sullivan temporarily extended the protection covering the names of the larger pool summoned for jury duty from July 20 through July 24. Those names will remain impounded for another 10 days because of concerns about juror safety.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Clancy-fixated Illinois mom sang 'Wizard of Oz' tune after allegedly killing 2-year-old son: report
summary: Corie Walsh allegedly sang a "Wizard of Oz" tune during questioning after being charged with first-degree murder in her son Barrett Walsh's death.
story: A tragic child murder case in Illinois has prosecutors raising questions about a potential copycat link to the Lindsay Clancy trial. Corie Walsh is accused of murdering her two-year-old son Barrett in Frankfort, Illinois. Senior correspondent Mike Tobin reports on the disturbing details of the investigation, including the defendant's alleged statements to police.

Corie Walsh, the woman who obsessed over the Lindsay Clancy case and allegedly killed her 2-year-old son, sang a rendition of a Wizard of Oz classic while being questioned by investigators, according to reports.

Walsh, 40, who allegedly told officers she killed her son because she believed he was the "devil" and the "anti-Christ," belted out "Follow the Yellow Brick Road" from the movie classic, according to court documents obtained by The Sun.
She is charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the death of her son, Barrett Walsh, who was found hanging lifeless from a rafter in the basement of their suburban Chicago home.
ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY

A family portrait showing Corie Walsh, left, alongside her booking mugshot following her arrest on first-degree murder charges in Will County, Illinois. Walsh reportedly sang a rendition of "Follow the Yellow Brick Road" from "The Wizard of Oz" during police questioning. (Facebook/Corie Walsh;Will County Detention Facility)
The boy was discovered by his two siblings on Sept. 1 as they returned home from school. Upon arrival, responding police officers found a neighbor performing CPR on Barrett.
While speaking with detectives, Walsh reportedly went on an unhinged rant and singing her own version of "Follow the Yellow Brick Road."
LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY
Corie Walsh, top left, pictured with her husband and children wearing matching holiday pajamas on a couch. (Facebook/ Corie Walsh)
Walsh’s attorney, Andrea Lyon, said her client was "psychotic" and rejected any connection between her interest in the Clancy case and the alleged killing.
"She was psychotic. And this is not a first-degree murder," Lyon told reporters.
Before the killing, Walsh had become "very invested" in the Clancy murder trial, which involved the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children.

Lindsay Clancy looks on as jurors enter the courtroom during Clancy's murder trial at the Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on Sept. 4, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

She had discussed the case in text messages with her friends as recently as the morning she allegedly killed her son.
Fox News Digital's Greg Wehner contributed to this report.

title: AG Blanche unveils federal charges against 160 defendants in pandemic relief sweep
summary: The Justice Department announced 160 arrests tied to over $245 million in COVID fraud losses, plus a $10 million childcare scheme in California.
story: Fox News' Chanley Painter reports on the capture of Elaine Angene Escoe, a COVID-19 fraud fugitive, in Jamaica. Escoe is accused of fraudulently obtaining over $32 million in taxpayer-funded COVID-19 relief funds and fled the country in 2025. FBI Director Kash Patel highlights the ongoing success of the 'Most Wanted Fraudster' list.

The Justice Department has charged dozens of people for suspected fraud related to the COVID-19 pandemic that resulted in hundreds of millions of dollars in losses, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Tuesday.

Speaking with reporters in the White House Rose Garden, Blanche said that between mid-June and September, federal prosecutors from across the country helped facilitate the arrests of 160 criminal defendants, including around 80 who were newly charged over suspected COVID fraud in Missouri and neighboring states.
The suspected crimes involved more than $245 million in losses, Blanche said.
WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD
Attorney General Todd Blanche has announced charges against dozens of people connected to suspected COVID-19 relief fraud. (Jacquelyn Martin/AP Photo)

In addition, federal prosecutors in Southern California announced on Tuesday that 12 defendants operating at-home childcare facilities were charged with fraudulently collecting more than $10 million in government childcare payments, despite the operators having few or no children attending their facilities.
All 12 defendants were naturalized citizens from Syria, Afghanistan, Sudan, Iraq and Somalia.
EXCLUSIVE: VIDEO SHOWS MICHIGAN LAWMAKER TOURING DAYCARE IN $1.1M TAXPAYER FUNDING PROBE
"If you knowingly break the law, you will be held accountable," Blanche said.
Some of the defendants were allegedly not even in the U.S. when they allegedly submitted claims for childcare payments.

One defendant, Turkiya Alawad, 63, was found to be outside the U.S. between Jan. 1, 2024, and Jan. 30, 2024. However, they submitted and collected childcare payments for the dates she was not away, prosecutors said, according to The Associated Press.
MINNESOTA'S EYE-POPPING SUBSIDY PAYMENTS TO NINE DAYCARE CENTERS EXPOSED AFTER LAST WEEK'S FED RAIDS

The alleged daycare fraud case in California is larger than the one involving Feeding Our Future, which submitted roughly $4.6 million in claims to the Child Care Assistance Program in Minnesota, according to The AP.
The California case is even larger than the infamous Feeding Our Future case in Minnesota, according to The AP. (Photo by Shari L. Gross/Star Tribune via Getty Images)
The Trump administration has prioritized investigating and prosecuting fraud and abuse of government programs.

title: Seven noncitizens charged in North Texas election-integrity investigation
summary: The charges come as the Trump administration expands its election-integrity efforts.
story: Fox News correspondent Brooke Taylor gets an exclusive ride-along look with Homeland Security as agents ramp up arrests of immigrants who participated in voter fraud on 'The Story.'

Seven noncitizens have been charged in North Texas as part of a sweeping federal election-integrity operation, as the Trump administration ramps up its push to investigate and prosecute election-related crimes ahead of the midterms.

Fox News exclusively joined Homeland Security Investigations as federal agents carried out arrests in the Dallas–Fort Worth area, getting a firsthand look at how investigators are identifying and pursuing suspected cases of noncitizen voting.
U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Texas, Ryan Raybould, announced that six defendants were indicted on Sept. 10, while a seventh was charged with a criminal complaint the following day.
Federal agents arrested six of the defendants over the following several days, while a seventh, who had been considered a fugitive, surrendered to federal authorities.
Voters cast ballots at a polling station during an election. (iStock)

"One of the individuals, an illegal alien from Mexico, actually was a 2023 convicted felon for lying on a passport application," Raybould said. "So this person has already interacted with our office, the Department of Justice, and chose to then again commit a serious federal violation."
In an exclusive one-on-one with Fox News, Raybould said the seven cases are only the beginning of his office’s efforts.
Earlier this month, the DOJ charged five people in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Wisconsin in cases involving alleged illegal voting or fraudulent registration during the 2022 or 2024 elections.
"It’s important to clean up our elections and make sure that they’re free and fair," Raybould told Fox News.

"And my job as U.S. attorney is to prosecute cases and controversies. And so if fraud happens, whether it’s our elections, our health care fraud system, stealing from the American taxpayer, I’m going to go after it."
Raybould said prosecutors are focused on whether federal law was broken, not which candidate received an allegedly illegal vote.
FBI ARRESTS SUSPECT ACCUSED OF PAYING LA HOMELESS TO FORGE SIGNATURE USING REGISTERED VOTERS' IDENTITIES

"We don’t even know who they voted for, frankly, like we don’t care," Raybould said. "You can vote for whoever. That is not what we are focused on, it's the act. You're not allowed to vote if you're an illegal alien."
The federal effort to identify potential noncitizen voters has drawn scrutiny from Democrats over how investigators are accessing and analyzing voter information.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, (D-N.Y.), and Sen. Alex Padilla, (D-Calif.), on Monday made public a complaint from an anonymous DHS whistleblower alleging that personnel working on the department’s "Unlawful Voter Initiative" were directed to access state voter records in ways that may violate state laws.
DHS has pushed back on those allegations.
The Department of Homeland Security seal displayed. (Getty Images)

"The Department accessed publicly available data from states’ voter rolls and cross-referenced them with known aliens in our systems. It’s not rocket science; it’s an easy step to secure our elections," a DHS spokesperson told Fox News.
Asked about the allegations, U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould defended investigators’ use of federal databases and publicly available information.
"HSI has access to databases, and they have a right to access that database," Raybould told Fox News.
"They also can cross-reference that database with publicly available information."
Raybould compared the investigative approach to health care fraud cases, in which federal authorities analyze government data to identify potential outliers for further investigation.
WHITE HOUSE UNLOADS ON VIOLENT ‘CRIMINAL ALIEN’ NABBED AFTER INVESTIGATORS UNCOVER ELECTION OFFENSE
"We look at Medicaid data to identify outliers all the time, to pick targets," Raybould said. "Everybody should be in favor of making sure that illegals do not vote in our elections.
Raybould said prosecuting election fraud should have bipartisan support.

"If someone is illegal, and they vote in an election, that draws down the value of the vote of American citizens, and so it also undermines our democracy, and the vote is absolutely critical," Raybould said. "It's how we elect our leaders. It's an important voice for American citizens when they get to cast the ballot."
American voters cast their ballots at a polling station during an election. (Reuters)
The seven non-citizens are charged with the following offenses:

Helen Sayen Adams, is a 67-year-old citizen of Nigeria and lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder) since May 2024, is charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. Adams allegedly falsely claimed U.S. citizenship on a Texas voter-registration application in June 2024 and voted in the November 2024 general election in Tarrant County. She later admitted she was not a U.S. citizen.Joshua Nmelichukwu Akpom, is a 27-year-old citizen of Nigeria and lawful permanent resident since 2016, charged with false statements in relation to naturalization. As alleged, Akpom falsely denied on his 2026 naturalization application that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship, registered to vote, or voted, despite registering in 2017 and voting in the 2018 general election. Due to the five-year statute of limitations, prosecutors relied on the naturalization offense rather than the voting conduct.Carlos Salas Barrios, is a 41-year-old Mexican citizen and lawful permanent resident since 2018, charged by complaint with allegedly voting by an alien in a Federal Election. Barrios unlawfully cast a provisional ballot in Tarrant County in the November 2024 general election despite not being a U.S. citizen and not being registered. Although the ballot was ultimately rejected, casting it was still unlawful under Texas and federal law.Khalwinder Singh Bhengura, is a 69-year-old citizen of India and lawful permanent resident since 2022, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. Bhengura falsely claimed U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in January 2024 and again when applying for a Texas driver's license later that year in August. He voted in the November 2024 general election and later admitted he knew he was not a citizen. He was arrested on Sept. 11.Celestin Katubadi, is a 20-year-old citizen of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and lawful permanent resident, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to vote. Katubadi cast a provisional ballot in Tarrant County during the November 2024 general election after falsely claiming U.S. citizenship on an affidavit of provisional-voter. Although his ballot was rejected, casting it was still unlawful by Texas and federal law.Rocio Thrasher, is a 38-year-old Mexican citizen and lawful permanent resident since 2017, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. According to the indictment, Thrasher allegedly falsely declared U.S. citizenship when registering in June 2024 and voted in the November 2024 general election. She later admitted knowing she was not a citizen.Moises Anwar Arellano Alba, is a 36-year-old illegal alien from Mexico ordered deported in July, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. He allegedly falsely claimed U.S. citizenship when applying for a Texas driver's license in 2023 and voted early in the 2024 general election in Dallas County despite being a noncitizen and convicted felon. He admitted in immigration proceedings that he had voted. Arellano Alba was a fugitive until this morning when he surrendered himself to federal agents.

Helen Sayen Adams, is a 67-year-old citizen of Nigeria and lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder) since May 2024, is charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. Adams allegedly falsely claimed U.S. citizenship on a Texas voter-registration application in June 2024 and voted in the November 2024 general election in Tarrant County. She later admitted she was not a U.S. citizen.

Joshua Nmelichukwu Akpom, is a 27-year-old citizen of Nigeria and lawful permanent resident since 2016, charged with false statements in relation to naturalization. As alleged, Akpom falsely denied on his 2026 naturalization application that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship, registered to vote, or voted, despite registering in 2017 and voting in the 2018 general election. Due to the five-year statute of limitations, prosecutors relied on the naturalization offense rather than the voting conduct.

Carlos Salas Barrios, is a 41-year-old Mexican citizen and lawful permanent resident since 2018, charged by complaint with allegedly voting by an alien in a Federal Election. Barrios unlawfully cast a provisional ballot in Tarrant County in the November 2024 general election despite not being a U.S. citizen and not being registered. title: Lindsay Clancy judge indefinitely impounds juror names, citing safety and 'divisive' attention
summary: Judge William Sullivan sealed juror names in the Lindsay Clancy mistrial case, citing safety concerns and unauthorized identification of jurors.
story: Paula Devlin, one of 11 jurors on the Lindsay Clancy trial who believed she was not criminally responsible for the deaths of her three children, explains the emotional toll of deliberations. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)
The judge in the Lindsay Clancy case has indefinitely sealed the jurors' names, citing safety concerns and what he called "significant and divisive attention" on the trial.

Judge William Sullivan issued the order on Monday and said while the court acknowledges that the jurors' names must be made available to the public, there is a "real and present" risk of harm to the jurors, stating he's impounding all names indefinitely until otherwise ordered.
Sullivan noted that there have been "identifications of jurors and their personal information without their permission" in explaining his reasoning for shielding the jurors' names.

"Some of the empaneled jurors have come forward and spoken to the media after the declaration of a mistrial on September 4, 2026. However, the majority of the jurors, deliberating and alternates, have maintained their anonymity, despite multiple requests to give statements," Sullivan wrote. "The Court concludes that there is a risk of immediate and irreparable injury should the list be made available to the public at this time."
LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR DENIES BIAS ALLEGATIONS, WANTS 'CONVERSATION STARTED' ABOUT WOMEN'S MENTAL HEALTH

Lindsay Clancy looks on as jurors enter the courtroom during Clancy's murder trial at the Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on Sept. 4, 2026. (Greg Derr / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

In a separate filing on Monday, Sullivan ordered the impoundment of the clerk's list of potential jurors for the Plymouth County Courthouse for July 20 through July 24, during jury selection for the trial, "based upon threats and concerns over juror safety."

"Immediate and irreparable injury and dangers to jurors and to the administration, is real and present," he wrote, sealing the names of the entire jury pool for people who were called to jury duty during that timeframe.
That order is set to expire in 10 days.

Clancy, 36, faced three counts of first-degree murder in connection with the slayings of her children — 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan — who were discovered strangled at the family's home in January 2023. title: Army veteran paratrooper who deployed to Iraq, Afghanistan before helping rescue Fox News reporter dead at 50
summary: Sean Michael Lee's cancer was linked to burn pits in Iraq and Afghanistan, ending a life devoted to rescuing thousands from war zones and disasters.
story: Fox News senior correspondent Benjamin Hall and combat surgeon Dr. Joe Aldrete discuss their participation in the Tunnel to Towers 10th annual tower climb at One World Trade Center. Hall, who was critically wounded in Ukraine, emphasizes climbing to raise money for Gold Star families. Dr. Aldrete, who performed life-saving surgery, praises Hall's resilience, underscoring the importance of hope and community support for military families.
Sean Michael Lee, an Army paratrooper who helped evacuate thousands from conflict zones after his service — including Fox News' Benjamin Hall — died Sunday after a battle with esophageal cancer.
Lee was a 20-year veteran of the Army, having served multiple deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan as a member of the Army's storied 82nd Airborne Division, according to his obituary.

"He was, to his core, a paratrooper. Long after he took off the uniform, the values forged there remained the organizing principles of his life: duty, loyalty, competence under pressure, and an unwavering commitment to the person beside him," his obituary reads.
AMERICA’S PROMISE TO OUR AFGHAN ALLIES IS STILL UNFINISHED FIVE YEARS LATER
Sean Michael Lee in uniform. (Sarah Verardo/The Independence Fund)

Lee spent the years after his military service continuing to help people. In 2021, as Afghanistan's government was collapsing, Lee worked to help evacuate thousands during a chaotic withdrawal as a member of the nonprofit group Save Our Allies.

Just a year later, Lee was in Poland helping deliver supplies to the frontline in Ukraine in the midst of Russia's invasion. It was there that Lee became a key part of extracting Fox News correspondent Benjamin Hall, who had been severely injured when Russian forces attacked his vehicle near Kyiv. Two members of Hall’s crew were killed in the attack.
BENJAMIN HALL TACKLES GRUELING ONE WORLD TRADE CENTER CLIMB ON PROSTHETIC LEGS TO HONOR FALLEN HEROES

"We got the call, we had just finished up a staff meeting with our folks back in the United States, and I can tell you that in about 90 minutes our guys were out the door and on the way," Lee explained to the Daily Caller during a 2022 interview.

Fox News correspondent Benjamin Hall visits "The Faulkner Focus" with host Harris Faulkner in New York City on March 15, 2023, to discuss his book, "Saved: A War Reporter’s Mission to Make It Home." (Roy Rochlin/Getty Images)
Lee also worked to help wounded veterans through The Independence Fund.

In 2024, Lee helped deliver life-saving supplies to survivors of Hurricane Helene in North Carolina. He lived out of a tent in the Tar Heel state as he helped deliver aid to communities where support systems had collapsed, according to his obituary.
LUKE COMBS AND ERIC CHURCH RAISE OVER $24.5 MILLION FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS AT STAR-STUDDED CONCERT FOR CAROLINA
Sean Michael Lee in front of a tent. (Sarah Verardo/The Independence Fund)
Most recently, Lee had been working under Secretary Doug Collins at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.

"Sean spent his life running toward the crisis. After more than two decades in uniform and multiple combat deployments, he continued that service through The Independence Fund, Save Our Allies and ultimately the Department of Veterans Affairs," Sarah Verardo, a founder of The Independence Fund and close friend of Lee's, told Fox News Digital.

"Whether evacuating Afghan combat interpreters and their families, helping establish field hospitals in Ukraine, or living out of his car to deliver aid in Western North Carolina, Sean went wherever he was needed most. His service knew no boundaries, and he never wanted fanfare or credit. He simply lived the ethos of ‘send me.'" Verardo said.
She also explained how Lee and her husband, a fellow member of the 82nd Airborne who was wounded in combat, forged a close personal bond.
Sean Michael Lee (C) pictured with Sarah Verardo. (Sarah Verardo)

"Sean walked alongside my husband for years following his catastrophic combat injuries and through his death, and for the better part of a decade, he was a constant presence in the lives of my three girls. He never missed a first day of school or a Halloween with us. Until his final breath, he remained that constant, living with us throughout his cancer battle and, even as his own world became smaller, still wanting to hear about dance recitals, science projects and all the ordinary details of their lives. He showed up for the defining moments and the ordinary ones because, to Sean, service was never a job or an assignment. It was simply who he was," she said.
"Sean was the definition of a quiet warrior. Our family has lost one of our own, and our nation has lost a patriot whose service never stopped," Verardo concluded.

He was part of the U.S. military's 2003 invasion of Iraq. He was also part of the storied Bravo Company in the 2-508 Parachute Infantry Regiment. Half of the company received Purple Hearts for an Afghanistan deployment that was documented in Ben Kesling’s book "Bravo Company: An Afghanistan Deployment and its Aftermath."
Lee's two best friends — Sgt. Michael Verardo and Sgt. Allen Thomas — both of whom deployed with him to Afghanistan, passed away before him.
Lee's cancer was the direct result of his exposure to the burn pits in Iraq and Afghanistan. He died at age 50.
VETERANS FACE SURPRISING THREAT AFTER CANCER DIAGNOSIS, STUDY REVEALS
Sean Michael Lee in Iraq. (U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) Defense Visual information Distribution Service (DVIDS))
"I can’t even begin to explain what the world has just lost," former MMA fighter and Special Forces sniper Tim Kennedy wrote in a post on Instagram.
"This country has lost one of the finest men ever to serve it," Kennedy's message continued.

"Sean redefined the word service. He did not just volunteer to put on the uniform and join the 82nd Airborne. He dedicated his entire life to other people. He put his life on the line more times than anyone can count. Wherever people needed help, you found Sean. Whenever I needed help, I found Sean," Kennedy wrote.
Sean Michael Lee of The Independence Fund pictured next to two men. (Sarah Verardo/The Independence Fund)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Lee's life "cannot be measured simply in years, deployments, jobs, or missions. It is measured in people who made it home because he went toward danger," his obituary, shared by Heritage Funeral & Cremation Services, says. "In wounded men carried to safety. In Afghan families given a chance to begin again. In communities that received help when they believed they had been forgotten. In veterans whose lives were better because he continued serving them after his own time in uniform ended. And in the children who simply knew him as Uncle Sean: the constant, fiercely protective man who showed up."

title: Attempted Trump assassin Thomas Crooks used 'Bob Dole' alias before anonymous donor paid for cremation: docs
summary: Thomas Matthew Crooks used the alias "Bob Dole" to order suspicious packages before the Butler, Pennsylvania, assassination attempt on Trump.
story: Former assistant FBI director Chris Swecker discusses newly released FBI documents detailing the behavior of would-be Trump assassin Thomas Crooks.

Thomas Matthew Crooks, the Pennsylvania man who killed a bystander and seriously wounded two others in a failed assassination attempt on President Donald Trump, had no friends as a teenager and used the alias "Bob Dole" while ordering suspicious packages before an anonymous donor paid for his body to be cremated, according to federal documents viewed by Fox News Digital.
SEND US A TIP

The records turned over to the Senate were first reported by the New York Post and show Thomas’ actions were a surprise to his family. The records were turned over to Sen. Chuck Grassley in March, and President Donald Trump was briefed.
His motive is still a mystery.

Crooks, 20, typically collected packages addressed to the Dole alias before his father, who worked late, came home.  He was shot and killed after opening fire at a Trump rally in July 2024. A family attorney told investigators that he had been cremated shortly thereafter — paid for by an anonymous donor, according to the documents.
HANNITY PROBES THE PSYCHOLOGY OF TRUMP'S WOULD-BE ASSASSIN AND A NEW WAVE OF RADICALIZED YOUTH ON FOX NATION

The family of Thomas Crooks leaves the house in Bethel Park, Penn., on Thursday, August 1, 2024. Crooks died while attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump in Butler on July 13. (Derek Shook for Fox News Digital)
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
After the shooting, his father, Matthew Crooks, took an early retirement, and his mother, Mary Crooks, went on leave from work to process the situation.

The documents, compiled as part of the investigation into the 2024 shooting at a Trump rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, also include interviews with his father, who told FBI agents the gunman "never identified anyone as a friend throughout middle school and high school."

Thomas Matthew Crooks was a 20-year-old from Bethel Park, Pennsylvania, who attempted to assassinate former President Donald Trump during a 2024 campaign rally before being shot and killed by Secret Service agents. (Associated Press | Fox News Digital)
When agents interviewed Crooks' parents the day after the shooting, his father told investigators that although his son socialized with classmates, the gunman told him they were not his friends.
In the months before the shooting, Crooks's father observed him talking to himself. His father, who worked in the mental health field, said he did not see other signs of a potential mental illness.

Although his father described him as a straight-A student who scored a 1400 on his first SAT attempt, without studying, he told investigators he son feared he might not get into college and showed a change of behavior between his freshman and sophomore years of high school. He became quieter and had a hard time speaking with teachers.

Then-Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump pumps his fist as he is rushed offstage by U.S. Secret Service agents after being grazed by a bullet during a rally on July 13, 2024 in Butler, Pennsylvania.  (Anna MoneymakerGetty Images)
SECRET SERVICE MISSED 'MULTIPLE OPPORTUNITIES' TO PREVENT TRUMP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT: WATCHDOG
At one point, he floated the idea of joining the military to work on nuclear submarines, but it was unclear how serious he was about that ambition.
After studying, he retook the SATs and scored over 1500, according to the documents.
Crooks adopted the Dole pseudonym after his father's checking account had been hacked and fraudulent gambling charges appeared, Matthew Crooks told investigators.

title: Pennsylvania man accused of plotting ISIS attack arrested with rifle and 190 rounds of ammunition: DOJ
summary: Jonathan Hunter Kramer allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS and acquired a semiautomatic rifle before FBI agents tracked him to a Pennsylvania hotel.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A 21-year-old Pennsylvania man accused of plotting a violent attack on behalf of ISIS was arrested after FBI agents tracked him to a hotel and seized a semiautomatic rifle, five magazines and 190 rounds of ammunition, federal prosecutors announced Tuesday.

Jonathan Hunter Kramer, of Valencia, had allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS, offered to distribute explosives manuals online and said he was preparing for his "mission" but still needed a weapon before agents moved in, according to a federal criminal complaint.

Kramer is charged with receiving a firearm and ammunition, knowing or having reasonable cause to believe they would be used to commit a felony or federal crime of terrorism, including providing or attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.
WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS
The U.S. Department of Justice logo is seen on a podium before a news conference on May 4, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

The FBI had been aware since a 2023 investigation of Kramer, at the time a minor, when he was charged and adjudicated delinquent in Pennsylvania for his role in a plot to carry out a mass-casualty attack and for possessing child sexual abuse material, according to the Justice Department.

Authorities began investigating him again after an anonymous tip came in on March 19, shortly after his release from a juvenile detention facility. The tipster said Kramer was ordering "mysterious" packages and "talking to his friends from before" his juvenile adjudication.
FBI agents seized a semiautomatic rifle from Kramer's hotel room, authorities said. (Department of Justice)

Investigators said Kramer was using the online name "Hamza Al Rashid," claiming an affiliation with ISIS and offering to share explosives manuals. He allegedly wrote about preparing for his "mission" and said he was missing a "weapon."
On Friday, FBI agents watched Kramer leave his home with a bag and take a rideshare to a store, where he bought a disposable phone, according to the complaint.

He then met another person in the parking lot, took a long black bag from the trunk of a vehicle and traveled to a hotel in Cranberry Township, where he paid cash for a room. Witnesses at the store and hotel said the bag made a metallic clicking sound when Kramer put it down.
After checking in, Kramer went to a sporting goods store, where agents saw him at the gun counter.
FBI ARRESTS WOMAN WHO ALLEGEDLY PLOTTED ISIS-LINKED ATTACK ON NEW YORK STATE CAPITOL BUILDING

Agents approached him when he returned to the hotel carrying two bags from the store. Searches of Kramer, his hotel room and his home turned up a semiautomatic rifle, five rifle magazines — two loaded and three capable of holding 30 rounds each — and 190 rounds of rifle ammunition, according to the complaint.
Three of the five rifle magazines seized by the FBI. (Department of Justice)
Agents also found a rifle scope and bipod, an entrenchment tool, pepper spray and about 30 knives. A handwritten note read, "DoNt look For me[.] IDK what I did buT I cant live In constant Fear[.]"
Attorney General Todd Blanche said the arrest came as Americans marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.
Attorney General Todd Blanche praised authorities who carried out the investigation and arrest. (Aaron Schwartz/Bloomberg via Getty Images, File)
"Their outstanding work thwarted this alleged attack before innocent lives could be lost," Blanche said.
FBI Director Kash Patel said Kramer had been "plotting a violent attack in support of ISIS," citing his online activity and acquisition of weapons.
Kash Patel, director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, speaks during a news conference at the Department of Justice in Washington, D.C., on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The Justice Department did not identify a specific target for the alleged attack.

title: GA man wanted after being filmed 'intensely interacting' with rubber duck in stranger's hot tub: 'Infatuated'
summary: Surveillance video captures a man trespassing into a stranger's hot tub and spending over 10 minutes "intensely interacting" with a rubber duck.
story: Philadelphia police are searching for a suspect wearing a Chucky mask who allegedly chased a jogger and asked if she was 'ready to die' in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Georgia police are searching for a man who police say was "infatuated" with a rubber duck in a stranger's hot tub.

The suspect is wanted for trespassing onto the homeowner's property and stealing their towels before fleeing the scene, according to the Chatham County Police Department, which said the man became "obsessed" with the rubber duck he found at the residence.

"He trespassed onto their property, used their hot tub, became obsessed with their rubber duck, then stole their pool towels. It's obviously not the biggest crime we've dealt with this month, but it has a lot of ick-factor. So, we'd like to find this guy so he doesn't do this to someone else," police wrote.
FLORIDA MAN WHO HAD SEXUAL ENCOUNTER WITH VACUUM CLEANER NEAR DISNEY WORLD TAKES NO CONTEST PLEA
Police said the man was caught on video becoming infatuated with a rubber duck. (Chatham County Police Department)
Police said that surveillance video from the home in the 9000 block of Whitefield Avenue shows the man trespassing between 2:15 a.m. and 5:30 a.m. on September 1.

Video footage shows the man swimming in the pool before hopping into the hot tub, where he became "infatuated" with a rubber duck and was seen "intensely interacting" with the toy, according to police.
"While in the hot tub, the man is caught on video becoming infatuated with a rubber duck. The video shows the man spending more than 10 minutes intensely interacting with the duck," police wrote.
Police said the suspect was obsessed with the homeowner's rubber duck. (Chatham County Police Department)

title: Georgia mayor, 23, ousted 10 months after making history as state’s youngest mayor
summary: Jayden Williams, 23, was removed by the Stockbridge City Council after allegations involving public funds and communications with an 18-year-old student.
story: Jayden Williams faced intense questioning during an investigative hearing over his communications with an 18-year-old high school student. (City of Stockbridge Government)

Georgia's youngest elected mayor was removed from office just 10 months after taking the job following allegations that he misused city funds and exchanged sexually suggestive messages and images with an 18-year-old high school student.
Jayden Williams, who recently turned 23, was impeached by the Stockbridge City Council in the city south of Atlanta after taking office in January.
"The City of Stockbridge confirms that the City Council has taken formal action concerning the Office of Mayor," the city said in a statement on Sunday. "The Mayor has been removed from office."

Williams was accused of using his city purchasing card for more than $4,000 in personal expenses, including restaurant meals, clothing, haircuts and a movie, according to Fox 5 Atlanta. He reportedly spent $2,600 on gas and used a city vehicle for personal purposes.
MASSACHUSETTS MAYOR CHARGED WITH WIRE FRAUD IN $1.5M COVID RELIEF SCHEME
Jayden L. Williams, 23, was removed from office on Sept. 12, 2026. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
The spending was reported after city workers noticed unusual transactions involving public funds and immediately notified management and the city’s legal team.

According to Williams’ testimony, he did not intend to use city funds and later repaid the money, Fox 5 reported. He further claimed the city-issued card looked similar to his personal card and said he later replaced the cards to avoid future confusion, the outlet reported.
FORMER DEMOCRATIC MAYOR OF STATE CAPITAL CITY PLEADS GUILTY FOR ROLE IN SIX-FIGURE REAL ESTATE BRIBERY SCHEME
Mayor Jayden Williams appears at a public investigative hearing on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. (City of Stockbridge Government/Facebook)

title: Construction rig collapses on 3 cars in Miami, traps workers as fire erupts
summary: A dramatic scene unfolded in Miami's popular Brickell neighborhood after heavy equipment crashed onto vehicles and a construction container, sending four people to the hospital.
story: Dramatic video shows a car engulfed in flames after a massive construction rig collapsed onto vehicles in Miami. (Credit: @CityofMiamiFire via X)

Four people were taken to the hospital Monday after a construction rig toppled onto three vehicles and a construction container in Miami, trapping two workers and igniting a vehicle fire, authorities said.
Miami Fire Rescue responded to the scene in the city's popular Brickell neighborhood near Southeast 12th Street and Brickell Bay Drive after the drilling rig collapsed at around 8 a.m.
"Miami Fire Rescue responded after a drilling rig fell onto three vehicles near SE 12 Street and Brickell Bay Drive," Miami Fire Rescue said in a post on X.
"The Technical Rescue Team units worked to safely free two trapped victims in a crushed container. Fortunately, the 4 patients transported were in stable condition."
MIAMI WAITRESS ACCUSED OF EXTORTION & THREATENING TO SEND INTIMATE PICS AFTER LEARNING SHE WAS THE OTHER WOMAN
Four people were taken to the hospital Monday after a construction rig toppled onto three vehicles and a construction container in Miami. (@CityofMiamiFire via X)
Firefighters rescued two construction workers, ages 27 and 29, who were trapped inside the crushed construction container, Miami Fire Chief Robert Hevia said during a news conference.
Crews simultaneously extinguished a fire that erupted after the rig crushed a BMW, Hevia said.

"To be able to see the crane falling, pull the car in reverse and pop out of the back while the car’s on fire, really incredible," he said, describing how the BMW's driver managed to escape the burning vehicle.
The rig also crushed two unoccupied parked vehicles, he said.
CRANE ARM COLLAPSES INTO MIAMI CONDO ROOFTOP POOL AREA AS WORKERS CLING TO DANGLING STRUCTURE
Firefighters extinguished a blaze that erupted after the rig crashed onto a BMW, according to Hevia. (@CityofMiamiFire via X)

The two workers, the 47-year-old rig operator and the BMW driver were all taken to local hospitals with minor injuries, he said. Hevia also said all 18 construction workers at the site were accounted for.

"It was a very complex scene with a fire that was occurring, our crews were putting out the fire and our technical rescue team working simultaneously to cut through the Conex box, the construction box, and they were able to successfully extricate the two victims," Hevia said.
Earlier Monday, the Miami Police Department urged motorists to avoid the area.

"Due to a crane collapse, Brickell Bay Drive is currently closed between SE 12th Street and SE 13th Street. Motorists are encouraged to avoid the area, seek alternate routes, and expect delays. Please use caution and follow the direction of officers on scene," Miami Police wrote on X.
ONLYFANS MODEL COURTNEY CLENNEY SENTENCED TO SIX YEARS IN BOYFRIEND’S KILLING
Officials have not said what caused the rig to collapse. (@CityofMiamiFire via X)
Officials have not said what caused the collapse. Hevia said the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is investigating the incident.
According to NBC 6 South Florida, the collapse occurred at the site of billionaire Ken Griffin's planned Citadel headquarters.

title: Trump brings new heat to controversial UN agency as alleged Hamas ties engulf scores of employees
summary: UN Watch says UNRWA completed at most 13 of 50 reforms, accusing the agency of counting draft policies and pilot programs as finished overhauls.
story: Stéphane Dujarric tells Fox News Digital UNRWA is implementing the Colonna recommendations as a new report questions how many reforms were actually carried out. (Credit: UNTV)

President Donald Trump recently amplified a report about a U.S. government investigation that referred more than 100 current or former UNRWA employees over alleged ties to Hamas — as a new watchdog report accuses the UN agency of overstating how much it has reformed.

The scrutiny, which included Trump sharing the report on Truth Social in August, comes as Geneva-based UN Watch released a report Monday challenging UNRWA’s claim that it has completed 41 of the 50 reforms recommended by an independent review led by former French Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna.

UN Watch says that when it compared UNRWA’s claims with what Colonna actually recommended, at most 13 of the 50 reforms had been completed as prescribed. The group argues that UNRWA repeatedly counted drafting policies, launching pilot programs or creating plans as completed reforms even when full implementation had not occurred.
UN AGENCY ACCUSED OF HAMAS TIES SEES ANOTHER EUROPEAN NATION CUT FUNDING
United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) building in Gaza, June, 2023. (Ahmed Zakot/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

"UNRWA is grading its own homework—and giving itself credit for reforms that exist mainly on paper," UN Watch Executive Director Hillel Neuer told Fox News Digital. "A policy is not a reform if it is ignored, unenforced or blocked by staff unions dominated by Hamas."

Among the examples cited in the report is staff vetting. UNRWA lists a "Commercial Vetting Pilot & Costed Plan" as completed, along with other screening measures. UN Watch argues that a pilot and implementation plan do not amount to a fully operational outside vetting system.

The report also challenges UNRWA’s education reforms. UNRWA lists systematic textbook reviews and randomized classroom inspections among completed steps, while a policy prohibiting problematic educational content is still described as "in progress."

Colonna herself said when presenting her review in April 2024 that some educational content remained problematic, citing "glorification of jihad," incitement to violence and maps that did not show Israel, while calling for a zero-tolerance approach.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM
UNRWA's headquarters in Gaza City, Gaza on Feb. 21, 2024. (Dawoud Abo Alkas/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Pressed by Fox News Digital at Tuesday’s UN briefing over who independently verifies whether the reforms are actually working on the ground, UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric defended the process.
"It is not just checking boxes for the sake of checking boxes," Dujarric said, "It’s about the implementation of those things."
Dujarric said UNRWA regularly reports to the General Assembly, holds integrity meetings open to member states and gives governments opportunities to scrutinize what the agency is doing.
WATCHDOG DEMANDS APOLOGY AFTER UN MEMORIAL ERRONEOUSLY HONORS HAMAS TERRORIST

This picture taken during a media tour organised by the Israeli army on February 8, 2024, shows Israeli soldiers inside an evacuated compound of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) in Gaza City. (Jack Guez/AFP via Getty Images)
Asked specifically about staff screening, he said UNRWA relies in part on countries where it operates.

"We rely on the member states also, where we operate, who have the capacity to check people to do so," Dujarric said, adding that UNRWA shares staff lists with Israeli, Jordanian, Lebanese and Syrian authorities. "If there are concerns, they need to be shared directly with UNRWA. When they are, they take action."

The Colonna review was commissioned by UN Secretary-General António Guterres in February 2024 after allegations that UNRWA employees had participated in the Oct. 7 attacks. Guterres accepted all 50 recommendations in April 2024 and agreed with UNRWA leadership to establish an action plan to implement them.
Neuer rejected the idea that the disagreement is merely about terminology.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Heavy machinery operates as Israeli forces dismantle the Jerusalem headquarters of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA), in East Jerusalem, Jan. 20, 2026. (Ammar Awad/Reuters)

"This is not a semantic disagreement over the meaning of ‘completed,’" he said. "UNRWA says the job is done, yet teachers tied to terrorist organizations remain in classrooms, Hamas-dominated unions obstruct discipline, and children continue to be exposed to incitement. Those are real-world consequences, not technicalities."

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Norway faces backlash over 'deeply racist' proposal to jail citizens for West Bank business
summary: Critics say Norway's proposed trade ban on Israeli settlements in Judea and Samaria effectively singles out Jews, calling the possible legislation racist.
story: US Amb. Mike Huckabee warns of negative impact over UK plan to ban Israeli West Bank settlement goods, speaking to 'BBC World Service Newsday.' (Credit:  'BBC World Service Newsday' via Reuters.)

Critics are slamming Norway over new legislation that they say singles out Jews. The proposed law could send individuals to prison for up to three years for knowingly conducting certain forms of business with Israeli communities in the West Bank.

The proposal, introduced by Norway’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, would prohibit the importation of goods originating in Israeli communities in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem and the exportation of goods to those communities. It would also restrict certain real estate transactions, construction and engineering services and investments in businesses headquartered and operating there.

Intentional violations could result in fines, imprisonment for up to three years or both, while negligent violations could carry fines, imprisonment for up to six months or both, according to Section 7 of the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ official consultation document.
ISRAEL’S E1 PLAN EXPLAINED: THE JERUSALEM-AREA CORRIDOR SPARKING INTERNATIONAL BACKLASH

(L-R) Palestinian Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas, and Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide addressed the media following the 9th Global Alliance for the Two-State Solution Meeting and the Ad Hoc Liaison Committee (AHLC) Meeting, focusing on international aid for Palestinians and the revitalization of the peace process. (Dursun Aydemir/Anadolu via Getty Images)
The measure remains under public consultation, with responses due Sept. 19, and has not yet been enacted.
Israeli Ambassador to the United Nations Danny Danon condemned the proposal in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Norway’s proposal to criminalize trade with Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria is the latest expression of their obsessive and openly hostile policy toward Israel. Instead of contributing to peace or regional stability, Norway has chosen political grandstanding, selective outrage and punitive measures against Israel," Danon said. "This approach damages bilateral relations, encourages rejectionism, and exposes just how detached Norwegian policy has become from the realities of the Middle East."
The Israeli Foreign Ministry’s Northern Europe Department also referred Fox News Digital to a statement it posted on X condemning the proposal.
US AMBASSADOR HUCKABEE SLAMS EXTREME GROUP OF ISRAELI SETTLERS FOR SEIZING PALESTINIAN HOMES ON WEST BANK
The Libi Infrastructure and Construction factory in the Israeli settlement of Shilo in the West Bank, April 30, 2026. (Reuters/Ammar Awad)

"Norway’s legislative proposal to criminalize trade with Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria is the latest example of the Norwegian foreign minister’s obsessive anti-Israel activism on the global stage. Norway has repeatedly chosen to sacrifice its bilateral relationship with Israel in favor of one-sided rhetoric and hostile actions that serve domestic interests, undermine efforts to reach peaceful solutions, and are completely detached from the reality in the Middle East."

In response to a request for comment from Fox News Digital, Norway’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs referred the outlet to its June 19 press release announcing the proposed legislation. The release states that Israeli settlements violate international law and undermine prospects for a two-state solution in which Israelis and Palestinians can live in peace and freedom.

"By proposing legally binding prohibitions, the government makes it clear that Norwegian citizens and Norwegian companies must not profit from or support activities that help sustain Israel’s unlawful settlement activity in Palestine," Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said in the release.
Eide also said the settlements contribute to "displacement, extreme violence and a situation that makes a peaceful solution impossible."
UN AGENCY ACCUSED OF HAMAS TIES SEES ANOTHER EUROPEAN NATION CUT FUNDING
The West Bank, also known as Judea and Samaria, is home to some 500,000 Israelis. (Mahmoud Illean/AP)

The ministry cited United Nations Security Council findings and International Court of Justice advisory opinions supporting its position on the settlements’ illegality. It said the proposed restrictions would cover imports and exports, property purchases, certain property-related services and acquisitions of businesses with headquarters and production in the settlements, while safeguarding legitimate Palestinian activities and humanitarian assistance.

The proposed legislation would exempt humanitarian activities, as well as transactions the government determines have "sufficient Palestinian ties" and do not contribute to the construction, expansion or maintenance of Israeli communities.

Dag Juliussen, national director of the Norwegian branch of the International Christian Embassy Jerusalem, said that the exemption could permit business with Palestinian residents while criminalizing comparable transactions involving Jewish residents in the same territory.

Israel's Ambassador to the UN Danny Danon (bottom-R) speaks during a General Assembly meeting to vote on a two-state solution to the Palestinian question at United Nations headquarters on Sept. 12, 2025 in New York City. (Angela Weiss /AFP via Getty Images)

"The bill is based on a fundamentally misguided understanding of the Middle East conflict, which in turn rests on a rewriting of history," Juliussen said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "In addition, such a law would effectively serve as a reward for terrorism and, at its core, is deeply racist toward Jews."
CHRISTIAN ZIONISTS TAKE ON ANTI-ISRAEL ‘PROPAGANDA’ FROM BIBLICAL HEARTLAND

The consultation document does not characterize the proposal as targeting Jews. Instead, it says the measure is intended to prevent commercial activity that helps maintain Israeli communities beyond the pre-1967 lines, while shielding qualifying Palestinian commerce and humanitarian assistance.

Under the proposal, exemptions would be evaluated according to the people involved who benefit from the transaction and whether the activity contributes to the construction, expansion or maintenance of an Israeli community.

Juliussen said purchasing agricultural products from Muslim, Christian, Arab or Bedouin residents could be permitted, while purchasing similar products from Jewish residents could become a criminal offense. He argued that the determining factor would effectively be the identity of the seller.
Norway formally recognized a Palestinian state in 2024 and has become one of Israel’s strongest European critics since the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of Oct. 7, 2023.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Juliussen warned that the proposed legislation would not bring Israelis and Palestinians closer to peace but could instead deepen divisions and encourage extremist forces in the region.
