A satellite imagery shows Bab el Mandeb Strait, as Iran threatens using Yemen's Houthi allies to shut this gateway to the Red Sea, in this handout picture dated July 12, 2026. (Nasa Worldview/Handout via Reuters)

Oil markets were already responding to the widening regional threat Thursday. Brent crude jumped more than 5% to $106.60 a barrel by late Thursday morning, while U.S. crude climbed above $100 for the first time since May, according to Reuters.
Reuters contributed to the story.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Fire aboard cargo ship undergoing repairs at busy Chinese port leaves 25 people dead, five more injured
summary: A cargo ship called the Ocean Melody caught fire during repairs at Qingdao port, killing 25 of the 42 people on board the Liberian-flagged vessel.
story: The ship was docked at the port of Qingdao for repairs when a fire started, reportedly killing at least 25 people and injuring five others. (UGC via AP)
A cargo ship docked for repairs at a port on the northeastern coast of China caught fire Thursday, killing at least 25 people who were on board at the time, according to Chinese state media.

The ship was being fixed by Beihai Shipbuilding Co. in the port of Qingdao — one of the country's major shipping hubs — when it caught fire at approximately 11:15 a.m. local time, the Xinhua news agency reported.

A total of 42 people were on the vessel at the time of the blaze, and 12 of them were safely rescued, Xinhua reported. Five others were injured and taken to the hospital, where they are in stable condition.
CARGO SHIP ATTACKED BY SMALL CRAFT NEAR STRAIT OF HORMUZ, UK MARITIME AGENCY SAYS
In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, a cargo ship is seen after it caught fire at a port in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province, on Sept. 10, 2026. (Li Aoqiu/Xinhua via AP)
Photos released by Xinhua identified the ship as the Ocean Melody. The ship-tracking website VesselFinder lists it as sailing under the Liberian flag.
The Associated Press reported that the fire was extinguished at around 2:30 p.m., a little over three hours after it started. Videos online showed plumes of white smoke billowing from the ship.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Chinese authorities have not said what sparked the blaze while the vessel was undergoing repairs.
In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, firefighters and crews gather near the cargo ship on fire on Sept. 10, 2026. (Li Aoqiu/Xinhua via AP)
TIM SHEEHY EXPOSES A 'SCARY' SHIPBUILDING COLLAPSE THAT LEAVES THE US VULNERABLE TO CHINA

China’s President Xi Jinping called for "intensified efforts" to provide support for those who were affected by the fire, Xinhua reported, adding that Premier Li Qiang said "trapped people" needed to be rescued.
Xi also called for ensuring "preventive measures are thoroughly implemented" and "resolutely prevent major and catastrophic accidents."
Aerial view of the illuminated Qingdao Qianwan Container Terminal at night on Sept. 6, 2026, in Qingdao, Shandong Province of China. (VCG/VCG via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Beihai Shipbuilding is a subsidiary of the state-owned China State Shipbuilding Corporation, the world's largest shipbuilder. According to the company's website, its primary businesses are shipbuilding and ship repair.

Qingdao, in China's Shandong province, is one of the country's busiest ports and a major center for shipbuilding, shipping and international trade. The port handles millions of containers each year and is home to several large shipyards.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: How 9/11 transformed synagogue security into a new reality for the Jewish community
summary: FBI data shows Jews face 63% of religiously motivated hate crimes as communities prepare for Rosh Hashanah on Friday, Sept. 11 amid rising threats.
story: Yeshiva University President Rabbi Ari Berman joins 'America's Newsroom' to discuss the rise of antisemitism in New York City following a hate crime attack at a Manhattan synagogue. Berman outlines campus security preparations prior to the start of classes as data shows 860 incidents in the city and nearly 1,200 statewide.

At sundown on Friday, Sept. 11, as America marks 25 years since the terrorist attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people, Jewish families across the country will welcome in Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish new year marking 5787.
They will enter synagogues at the moment of peak annual attendance, walking past armed guards, security cameras, secured doors and bag checks.
The convergence brings into focus how the Sept. 11 attacks transformed security in American synagogues and helped create the national infrastructure that now protects Jewish life.
FOX NEWS MEDIA ANNOUNCES EXTENSIVE 9/11 ANNIVERSARY COVERAGE FROM GROUND ZERO, PENTAGON AND SHANKSVILLE

An NYPD Mobile Command Unit stands outside of Temple Emanu-El on 65th Street near Central Park in New York City, May 22, 2025. This is part of an increase in security at Jewish organizations nationwide after an Israeli couple was killed in Washington, D.C. (Kevin C. Downs for Fox News Digital)

When Rosh Hashanah began six days after the attacks in 2001, a security guard stationed outside a synagogue was still unusual. Twenty-five years later, security is no longer an occasional precaution. It has become a permanent precondition of Jewish communal life.

"The confluence of events, the 25th anniversary of 9/11 and Rosh Hashanah, is really very meaningful to us," Eric Fingerhut, president and CEO of Jewish Federations of North America, told Fox News Digital. "If you trace the evolution of the security situation for the Jewish community in North America, you see that 9/11 really was a major turning point."

Before the attacks, Fingerhut said, synagogues may have relied on police to direct traffic during the High Holidays or installed basic alarm systems, but there was no widespread belief that Jewish communities needed protection from threats to their physical safety.
Law enforcement respond to a call at Temple Israel synagogue, Thursday, March 12, 2026, in West Bloomfield Township, Mich. (Corey Williams/AP Photo)

"That changed on 9/11," he said. "The Jewish community understood quite clearly that the people who attacked the World Trade Center and the Pentagon were attacking America that day, but they had a special animus for the Jewish community and the Jewish people."

Fingerhut said that shift led Jewish Federations of North America to help create the Secure Community Network after 9/11, giving communities a model for protecting Jewish institutions and a unified channel to federal law enforcement.

For generations, Rosh Hashanah preparation meant apples and honey, prayer books and the shofar. Now the checklist also includes secured entrances, emergency plans and congregants standing watch while their neighbors pray.
The price of that new reality is staggering.
MARYLAND SYNAGOGUE SUES COUNTY OVER LAW RESTRICTING CONCEALED CARRY NEAR HOUSES OF WORSHIP
Two flags flutter on a fence in front of Lower Manhattan and One World Trade Center at the Tear Drop 9/11 Memorial at sunset on June 13, 2026, in Bayonne, New Jersey. (Gary Hershorn/Getty Images)

A national study by Jewish Federations of North America found that Jewish communal institutions spend an estimated $1 billion annually on security. Based on an examination of more than 4,500 institutions, that amounts to nearly $2.8 million every day simply to keep Jewish life open and accessible.
The organization leads the national initiative placing professional security directors across all 141 Federation communities.
Rabbi Chaim Steinmetz, senior rabbi of Congregation Kehilath Jeshurun on Manhattan’s Upper East Side, described the contrast on his own block.

"If you walk past the churches on our block, the doors are wide open, inviting people in," Steinmetz told Fox News Digital. "But at our synagogue, there are security cameras, a double door system and a line of guards outside, at the cost of untold thousands of dollars."

That security is no longer reserved for major institutions or large cities. From New York and Florida to Michigan and Los Angeles, ordinary worshipers are training in situational awareness, access control, surveillance detection, emergency response and coordination with law enforcement.
A close-up image of a Jewish man wearing a traditional tallit (prayer shawl) and tefillin during morning prayers. (iStock)

The Community Security Service, or CSS, said more than 20,000 people completed its training in 2025. Of those, 6,100 volunteers protected 440 synagogues and nearly 100 Jewish events, logging more than 300,000 guard hours across 24 states.
The Secure Community Network (SCN) provides national intelligence and coordination. In 2025, it recorded 4,400 incident reports, trained 40,000 people and made 851 referrals to law enforcement.

"While the threat environment accelerates, our community has never been more prepared, informed or engaged," Michael Masters, SCN’s national director and CEO, told Fox News Digital. "This year our Duty Desk logged nearly 3,200 threat incidents, pacing ahead of last year."
Steinmetz said threats to the Jewish community "exploded after Oct. 7th," adding that "the hatred of Israel encourages antisemites to come out of the woodwork."

The FBI recorded 1,528 hate crime incidents targeting Jews in 2025, representing 63% of the nation’s 2,408 religiously motivated incidents. Jews comprise roughly 2% of the U.S. population, yet incidents targeting Jews represented 14% of all hate crimes reported nationwide.
ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE ESCALATES AS DEADLY WEAPON ATTACKS SURGE IN 2025: REPORT

Jewish students at El Camino Real Charter High School during a walkout protesting antisemitic incidents at the Woodland Hills school on Tuesday, Feb. 2024. (Sarah Reingewirtz/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images)

During the first eight months of 2026, major crime fell 6.2% across New York City, while confirmed hate crimes targeting Jews rose 8%, from 212 to 229, according to new NYPD figures. That averages nearly one such crime every 25 hours.

Fox News Digital contacted NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch about the department’s High Holiday preparations. The NYPD said it will hold a briefing ahead of the holidays and provide additional security details at that time.

In neighboring New Jersey, the state Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness (NJOHSP) said it is coordinating with the state Attorney General’s Office, New Jersey State Police, the FBI’s Newark field office, local law enforcement and community partners.
"Together, we are protecting houses of worship, helping ensure every New Jerseyan can practice their faith without fear, and keeping New Jersey safe and secure," NJOHSP said.
The coordination follows recent attacks on Jewish institutions.

On Aug. 14, a man was charged with allegedly disrupting a Friday night service attended by approximately 375 people at Manhattan’s Central Synagogue, damaging ceremonial candlesticks and assaulting a congregant and security guard. The charges against include federal hate crimes and damaging religious property resulting in bodily injury.

Five months earlier, an attacker inspired by Hezbollah rammed a pickup truck carrying gasoline and fireworks through the doors of Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Michigan, according to the FBI. Armed with a rifle and hundreds of rounds, he struck one security guard and exchanged gunfire with others.
Inside were 140 children at the synagogue’s early childhood center. Every child and staff member escaped without physical injury and the guard survived.
For Steven Ingber, CEO of the Jewish Federation of Detroit, the assault remains a powerful reminder of the need for vigilance as families prepare to gather.

Members of the New York Police Department patrol in front of a synagogue on Oct. 13, 2023 in the Williamsburg neighborhood in the borough of Brooklyn in New York City. Security has increased in New York City in the wake of the Hamas attack on Israel and after a former leader of Hamas called for Friday the 13th to be a global Jihad day. (Stephanie Keith/Getty Images)

"We take the security of our community with the utmost seriousness, and, of course, the assault on Temple Israel remains fresh in our minds," Ingber said. "We will enter the High Holidays vigilant and prepared. But we will also enter them with confidence and pride."

Rabbi Aaron Starr of Congregation Shaarey Zedek in suburban Detroit, who also serves as president of the Michigan Board of Rabbis, said Jewish Michiganders are entering the new year "with a feeling of heaviness."

"From marking the 25th year since the terrorist attacks on 9/11 to marking six months since the terrorist attack on our community and especially our children, anxieties are heightened," Starr told Fox News Digital exclusively. "We enter with heaviness, but we are also filled with hope for a better tomorrow."
LOX & LOADED: JEWISH GUN GROUP PARTNERS WITH NRA AMID RISING ANTISEMITISM
"No family should have to weigh their safety against their faith," Fingerhut said.

Employing one full-time security guard costs an estimated $90,000 annually, according to Jewish Federations of North America. The organization is advocating for greater federal support through the bipartisan Jewish American Security Act, which would strengthen security assistance for at-risk nonprofit institutions.
For Jewish communities, the question is no longer whether security is necessary, but who will bear the growing cost of making worship possible.

A Bronx man was charged with multiple hate crimes after allegedly disrupting Shabbat services and attacking a congregant and security member at Central Synagogue in Manhattan, police said. (REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz)
SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER
Steinmetz called that cost "a vicious tax on the Jewish community," one "levied by the antisemites."
For Fingerhut, the purpose of security is not simply to prevent an attack. It is to ensure fear never determines whether a Jewish family participates in Jewish life.

"We do not want anyone to make the choice not to participate in Jewish life because they are afraid for their safety," Fingerhut said. "What we have learned is that the visible presence of security, and the real impact of that security, is what enables and encourages people to come out and participate in Jewish life."
Fingerhut’s message to Jewish communities in America and around the world was clear: do not retreat, but continue to "lean into Jewish life."
He said, "We will make sure that there is safety and security in place so that we can all feel confident in our involvement in Jewish life."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
That is the purpose, according to the experts, of every guard, camera and volunteer: not to turn a synagogue into a fortress, but to ensure that Jewish life continues inside.

Ariella Noveck is a journalist specializing in antisemitism and Middle East affairs, with extensive experience covering Jewish communities worldwide. She can be followed on X and Instagram @AriellaNoveck

title: Apple’s record night and Colbert’s Emmys wins highlight TV in transition
summary: Apple took home a total of 28 trophies, with a record 14 for freshman comedy “Widow’s Bay.”
story: Maybe it was watching Stephen Colbert get his final two “Late Show” Emmys engraved at the after-party. Or hearing the rowdy Apple TV contingent in the audience whoop it up every time “Widow’s Bay” notched another win.
But inside the Peacock Theater on Monday night, this year’s Emmy Awards felt like a transition to a new era of television.
As the TV Academy’s events crew rolled away the blue carpet, the event gave us plenty of moments to remember. Here are just a few ...
A host with assists

With an opening musical number starring New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson and a “Law & Order: SVU” skit starring Taylor Swift, host Mariska Hargitay called in plenty of favors from her famous friends to help lend the Emmys a little star power. Hargitay, the show’s first female host in 15 years, rotated through at least 10 wardrobe changes, including a “Game of Thrones”-style fur cape and black power suit. But the uniform she kept on all night was cheerleader for the medium of television, going so far as to repurpose a line from Nicole Kidman’s viral AMC Theatres commercial to say, “At the end of the day, we come to TV for magic.”

title: How Kraft Heinz is keeping its legacy brands affordable to cost-conscious shoppers
summary: For Kraft Heinz CEO Steve Cahillane, changes in the grocery marketplace demand a shift in strategy.
story: Years of high inflation have strained household budgets across America, putting a spotlight on the rising costs of necessities such as gas and groceries. They have also contributed to a shift in how consumers perceive value at the supermarket.
New research from McKinsey finds that Americans are increasingly turning away from name-brand foods to lower priced, private-label or store-brand products.
For Kraft Heinz CEO Steve Cahillane, these changes in the marketplace demand a shift in strategy.
“We can’t just rely on having a strong brand and saying that’s going to be enough,” he said in an interview on a tomato farm in Woodland, California, part of NBC’s “Business in America” initiative.
“Consumers have only so many dollars available for their food budget in a month’s time, and so you have to earn the right to be in that basket each and every day.”
In recent years, store brands have shed their traditional associations with lower quality ingredients and temporarily “trading down.”
Today, 85% of consumers believe private-label grocery products are just as good or better than those from name brands, McKinsey reports.

Kraft Heinz sells more than 200 brands, many of them household names such as Heinz ketchup, Kraft Mac & Cheese, Oscar Mayer meats, Capri Sun drinks, Miracle Whip spread, Velveeta, Philadelphia cream cheese and Kool-Aid.
But this is a challenging time to be in the name-brand food business. Last year, Kraft Heinz’s net sales in North America were down about 5% from 2024.
When Cahillane took the helm as CEO in January, he was tasked with turning the business around.
One part of that strategy, he said, is deploying promotional discounts more strategically.

“We’re working with our retail partners to make sure that at the beginning of the month, when consumers are really doing their big shops, that we’re out there with good offers across the board,” he said.
Consumers in general tend to have more spending power at the beginning of the month when government benefits such as SNAP are distributed, paychecks arrive and monthly budgets reset.
“Promotions can be an effective means by which to drive that initial purchase,” said Erin Lash, a senior director of consumer equity research at Morningstar.
But promotions can also create a new challenge: getting shoppers to come back once the deal is gone.
“Promotions can be kind of a slippery slope,” said Mark Mayer, associate professor of Marketing at Indiana University and a former Kraft Foods brand manager.
If customers “only buy your product when they can get it for a deal,” then the promotion defeats its purpose, he said.
Unlike store brands, a company like Kraft Heinz needs a pricing strategy that both appeals to shoppers and also protects the brand’s status.
“In general, competing on price is not great for established brands,” said Alexander Chernev, professor of marketing at the Kellogg School at Northwestern University.

Unless a company is specifically positioned from the outset as a discount brand, slashing prices can undermine a brand’s identity. This is especially true for legacy products like those in Kraft Heinz’s portfolio.
It requires Kraft Heinz to pull off a difficult balancing act: Making its products more affordable without diminishing the value of its brands.
Cahillane said that when it comes to pricing, Kraft Heinz is not lowering list prices across the board. Only where the economics make sense.
“The biggest price drop, where we’re bringing prices down, is most certainly in our coffee business,” which is home to brands like Maxwell House and Gevalia.
A drop in global coffee prices strengthens the economic case for price cuts. As of Wednesday, benchmark coffee futures were down 30% from a year ago.
Kraft Heinz is also offering some of their products in smaller sizes.

“This isn’t shrinkflation,” Cahillane said, “this is recognizing that if we’re selling a 32-ounce bottle of ketchup and that’s too much for a family… we have a smaller 8-ounce bottle at a very affordable price.”
It’s a strategy that has also been utilized by other major packaged food companies, including PepsiCo, Campbells and Mondelez, as they look to offer shoppers lower-priced options.
Ultimately, Kraft Heinz must give shoppers a reason to pay full price, Cahillane said. And quality is what will justify the premium.

“Value is affordability, but it’s also delivering the product quality and the promise that you’re making to consumers,” he said. “If they buy your brand, they’ll be receiving a value that they’re willing to pay for.”

title: U.S. accuses Russia of plot to kill a prominent dissident in Washington
summary: The Kremlin orchestrated a murder-for-hire plot against a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C., this summer, the Department of Justice has said, as it unsealed charges against five people it alleged were part of a “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem around the world.”
story: The Kremlin orchestrated a murder-for-hire plot against a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C., this summer, the Department of Justice has said, as it unsealed charges against five people it alleged were part of a “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem around the world.”

The five people charged are still at large, the DOJ said in the indictment unsealed late Tuesday, describing the wider operation being run by Russian intelligence as “brazen, aggressive, and far-reaching.”
The FBI said it had disrupted the plot, although officials did not detail how.

Since at least 2024, the network is alleged to have paid Americans and foreigners to spy on targets, “carry out targeted killings,” and “commit acts of terrorism against civilian and military infrastructure in European countries that are aligned, or perceived to be aligned, with Ukraine,” the DOJ said.

Asked for a response to the allegations by NBC News, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a daily briefing call with reporters that “until we have heard or seen any reasonable evidence and arguments based on at least something tangible, we do not consider it necessary to comment on this news.”
Russia has for decades been accused by Western governments of carrying out attempted and successful killings abroad. Despite substantial evidence, it has always denied these allegations.

The indictment did not name the intended victim in Washington. The DOJ lists the defendants as Yuri Khrameev, known as “Colonel Yuri,” 63, and his son Kirill Khrameev, 27, both of Russia; Oemis Romagoza Durruthy and Yaidel Delgado Suarez, known as “Viking,” both 35 and Cuban nationals; and Angel Eduardo Castro, 22, of Venezuela.
The indictment describes Durruthy as “an influential member of the Cuban diaspora living in Russia,” where it says Suarez and Castro also reside.
All face a conspiracy to finance terrorism charge. Yuri Khrameev, Suarez and Castro face an additional charge of conspiracy to commit murder for hire.
Yuri Khrameev is alleged to be a former Russian intelligence colonel, while his son is an officer in Russia’s Federal Security Service, or FSB.

Prosecutors allege the network recruited a Venezuelan citizen living in Brooklyn this summer, promising him between $1,000 and $1,500 to photograph and film two locations associated with the Washington target.

The man carried out the surveillance but declined an offer from Suarez and Castro of $40,000 to “eliminate” or “disappear” the target himself, prosecutors said. The alleged recruiters asked whether he knew somebody who would.
Suarez also offered substantial sums of money to other people in the U.S. to finish the job, the indictment said.

Messages quoted in the indictment show the conspirators allegedly referring to murder as “construction.” Surveillance instructions included putting the man’s phone into airplane mode and filming while passing the house.
Suarez allegedly said he also had people in Mexico who could carry out the killing, but they were delayed.
A second alleged plot involved a dissident believed to be living in Lithuania who the network accused of making derogatory statements about Russia.

In that case, a U.S. citizen was promised $200 to photograph the target’s address in 2025, then offered around $25,000 to kill him, prosecutors said. When he refused, Yuri Khrameev allegedly offered a “simpler job” — setting fire to a warehouse or attacking an electricity substation.
The purpose, Khrameev allegedly said, was to target “all the countries that are helping Ukraine.”
Durruthy, meanwhile, is accused of coordinating logistics for attacks in Prague in June 2024 and Lithuania that September.
Lithuanian authorities had publicly named Durruthy as wanted in January in a case involving attempts to burn military equipment intended for Ukraine, according to Lithuanian broadcaster LRT.

“These defendants allegedly operated as part of a global assassination network that reached into the United States, attempting to recruit U.S. citizens and foreigners to carry out killings at the behest of the Kremlin,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg.
“Actions like these represent a gross violation of our sovereignty and a threat to our national security.”
James C. Barnacle Jr., head of New York’s FBI office, said the agency “disrupted this operation through relentless work and rock-solid partnership.”

title: Saudi Arabia accuses Houthis of attacking Mecca, warns holy city is a ‘red line’
summary: Saudi Arabia has accused the Iran-backed Houthi rebels of attempting to attack Islam’s holiest city, declaring Mecca a “red line” in the escalating conflict.
story: Saudi Arabia has accused the Iran-backed Houthi rebels of attempting to attack Islam’s holiest city, declaring Mecca a “red line” in the escalating conflict.
The kingdom’s claim drew condemnation from across the Middle East, but no immediate sign of military support as fears grew of a return to all-out war between the key U.S. ally and the Yemeni rebels.

The Houthis swiftly denied targeting Mecca, saying their operations had targeted Saudi oil facilities and military bases, “far removed” from the sacred site of the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. They accused Saudi Arabia of spreading “fabrications and lies.”

The Houthis’ rapid ground advance in Yemen and aerial attacks on Saudi Arabia have shut down a crucial oil pipeline, threatened energy supplies through a second major shipping route and left the kingdom struggling to respond.

The mounting hostilities have threatened to open a second front in the Iran war, with oil and gas prices rising.  President Donald Trump has so far offered no sign of any U.S. plans to intervene in this new theater.

The United States on Wednesday upgraded its travel advisory to Saudi Arabia to Level 3 amid the escalating conflict, warning Americans to “reconsider travel” to the kingdom and banning government employees from travel near the Yemen border.

Saudi military spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said Wednesday that the country’s air defense forces had intercepted the drone south of Mecca just before 7 p.m. local time Tuesday (12 p.m. ET), according to a statement.

He emphasized that the security of the holy city and of pilgrims was a “red line,” warning there would be no hesitation to take “necessary and deterrent measures” against the Houthis, the statement said.
Mecca is known as the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad, with millions of Muslims from around the world making the pilgrimage to the holy city each year.

“While the Houthis and Saudi Arabia trade barbs over whether the target was Mecca or not,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at New America, a think tank based in Washington, D.C., who follows Yemen and the wider Gulf region, “what is clear is you’re seeing a real demonstration of the Houthis’ continued strategic depth.”
He added: “The fact that they were able to strike this deep in Saudi Arabia is really a signal toward their capacity, if not future intentions.”
The Iran-backed rebels have ramped up attacks on cities across the kingdom after also capturing a key Red Sea port city and island in their bid to gain control of the crucial Bab el Mandeb strait.

Oil prices have soared over fears that the Houthis could shut down the waterway, which has been a crucial transit route for Saudi Arabian oil exports with the Strait of Hormuz largely closed by Iran since the U.S. and Israel launched their war in late February.
The international benchmark, Brent crude, was at around $108 per barrel early Wednesday. The nationwide average cost of diesel fuel hit another all-time high of $6.31.
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the alleged Mecca attack as a “dastardly and heinous” act.
Sharif, who recently agreed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia, did not directly mention the Houthis in his statement, but reiterated Pakistan’s general support for the kingdom.
The U.S. conducted a deadly bombing campaign against the Houthis last year, but has shown little appetite for another.

Trump said over the weekend that the Houthis had called his administration and said they “don’t want to fight with us.” Speaking with reporters during a visit to Dublin on Saturday, he said he also spoke with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and maintained that everything would “work out fine and dandy” in the region.
The Houthis and the opposing coalition backing the internationally-supported Yemeni government have been fighting a civil war since 2014, with no clear resolution despite a truce agreed years ago.
The United Nations Security Council met Tuesday in an emergency session to discuss the rising violence in Yemen, the region’s poorest country, with member countries urging de-escalation.
The U.N. warned that the ongoing clashes between Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels have displaced at least 125,000 people since the start of September.

title: What to know about the victims of the NBC L.A. news helicopter crash
summary: Tributes began pouring in Wednesday after a deadly news helicopter crash in Los Angeles left three people dead.
story: Tributes began pouring in Wednesday after a deadly news helicopter crash in Los Angeles left three people dead.
The crash occurred just before 7p.m. local time on Tuesday in the Chatsworth area of the San Fernando Valley, as the news chopper was covering a separate road traffic accident.
Angel City Air operated the helicopter, which was affiliated with NBC Los Angeles.

The victims aboard the helicopter were identified as Eliana Moreno, a journalist familiar to viewers of the station and its Spanish-language sister station, Telemundo 52, and pilot George Marciniw. The pair began flying together in 2023.
A pedestrian on the ground was also confirmed to have died at the scene, officials said. Authorities have yet to identify the individual.
Zareh Sevanesian, who witnessed the crash, said the helicopter was swaying before it started losing altitude.
“It was just getting lower and lower and lower and lower,” he said on NBC’s “TODAY” show.
Add to Google
Add to Google
Eliana Moreno
Moreno, in her late 30s, was born in Orange County, south of L.A.
She graduated from Chapman University in the area with a degree in broadcast journalism and political science in 2010, NBC Los Angeles reported.
Moreno joined Angel City Air’s helicopter team the same year and has reported for multiple Southern California news outlets.

A seasoned aerial journalist who also reported in Spanish, Moreno was known on her official Instagram account as, “Eli in the heli,” due to her work. There, she shared pictures of her chickens and pet dogs and a video of her engagement to fiancée Robert Barrientos, in 2025. He did not immediately respond to NBC News’s request for comment. The pair ran a half-marathon together in May, after which she wrote: “I surpassed everything I thought I could ever do so let’s see what I do next!”
Moreno also frequently shared multiple images of herself in the news chopper, covering stories on the go, with one caption reading, “I have the best job in the world.”

Veteran NBC4 Los Angeles anchor Colleen Williams paid tribute to “dear colleagues” while on air Tuesday evening. Visibly emotional, she told viewers: “We are coming on the air with heavy hearts tonight because we lost valued friends and colleagues ... while on assignment tonight.”
“We are going to take a couple of minutes to think about that, process it,” she added, her voice shaking.
Lynette Romero, co-anchor of NBC L.A.’s morning newscast, said they were “heartbroken” and are thinking of the families of Moreno and Marciniw.

“They were both doing what they loved so much, and for me, that’s comfort in knowing how happy they were. They loved breaking news, and they loved being in News Chopper 4,” she said Wednesday on NBC’s “TODAY” show.
George Marciniw
Marciniw also grew up in southern California, where he graduated from Burbank High School in 1974, according to NBC L.A.
Marciniw is believed to have had over 30 years of flight experience. He often shared sunsets and scenic pictures from the area on what he dubbed a “news cruise” in the helicopter.

He often credited pictures on his official Instagram page to his companion and colleague, Moreno. “And that’s a wrap for Friday night as the heavy fog rolls in with Eliana Moreno,” he wrote, sharing an image of the chopper. In another, he posted a picture of the L.A. Dodgers stadium lit up brightly at night, captioned: “A few shots Eliana took as we flew over Dodgers after the game. “Go Dodgers.”
Many online paid tribute to Marciniw, detailing his professionalism and fun-loving spirit. “Fly high in the great beyond,” wrote one individual. “Total utter disbelief,” wrote another.
NBC Los Angeles and Telemundo 52 issued a joint statement expressing condolences for the pair.

“We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening,” the stations said. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives.”
The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration will begin investigating the cause of the helicopter crash.

title: 3 dead after NBC L.A. helicopter crashes while covering fatal bus collision
summary: An NBC Los Angeles helicopter was covering a Los Angeles Metro bus and a passenger vehicle collision, which killed two people and injured others, fire officials said.
story: A helicopter affiliated with NBC Los Angeles crashed while it was covering a fatal bus collision Tuesday evening, killing the photojournalist and pilot on board and one person on the ground, the station and officials said.

The aircraft crashed in a parking lot near a self-storage facility in the community of Chatsworth, in the San Fernando Valley, according to the L.A. Fire Department and news video on the ground from NBC Los Angeles.
Angel City Air operated the helicopter, and the news station said it had lost contact with those on board.

“We knew it was a news chopper, we knew we’d lost contact with our people out there, and we’ve just received the confirmation that, in fact, NewsChopper 4 went down just before 7 o’clock tonight in Chatsworth,” anchor Colleen Williams said.
“We’re going to take a couple of minutes to think about that, to process and to regroup,” Williams added, her voice becoming emotional.
Lynette Romero, co-anchor of NBC L.A.’s morning newscast, said they were “heartbroken” and are thinking of the families of Moreno and Marciniw.

“They were both doing what they loved so much and for me, that’s comfort in knowing how happy they were. They loved breaking news, and they loved being in News Chopper 4,” she said Wednesday on NBC’s “TODAY” show.
Angel City Air, which describes itself as “a full-service aerial production company,” did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday night.
Three people were dead at the scene, and two others were taken to the hospital, Fire Battalion Chief Rico A. Gross said at a late-night news conference. Their conditions were unavailable.
One of those killed appeared to be a pedestrian on the ground when the crash happened, Fire Capt. Branden Silverman said earlier.
Zareh Sevanesian, who witnessed the crash, said the helicopter was swaying before it started losing altitude.
“It was just getting lower and lower and lower and lower,” he said on NBC’s “TODAY” show.
Add to Google
Add to Google

NBC Los Angeles identified the victims aboard the helicopter as Angel City Air employees Eliana Moreno, an aerial photojournalist familiar to viewers of the station and its Spanish-language sister station, Telemundo 52, and pilot George Marciniw.

Moreno was born in Orange County, south of L.A., and graduated from Chapman University with a degree in broadcast journalism and political science in 2010, NBC Los Angeles reported. She joined Angel City Air’s helicopter team the same year and has reported for multiple Southern California news outlets.
Marciniw also grew up in Southern California, where he graduated from Burbank High School, the station said.
NBC Los Angeles and Telemundo 52 issued a joint statement expressing condolences.

“We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening,” the stations said. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives.”

The helicopter crash occurred after two people were killed and others were injured in a crash between a Los Angeles Metro bus and a passenger vehicle on Nordhoff Street, according to the fire department.
It said that the bus crash happened at 5:03 p.m. and that firefighters worked to free the trapped people and assess the bus passengers.
The helicopter was one of multiple aircraft covering the crash, NBC Los Angeles reported earlier.

Fire and police personnel were nearby, Silverman said. They rushed to the crash, reported shortly before 7 p.m., and found the helicopter engulfed in flames, which had spread to nearby parked vehicles, he added.
Witness Zareh Sevanesian was driving nearby with his wife, Allyona, when he saw the chopper’s unusual descent.
“As we were driving, I looked over to my left,” he said. “I saw the helicopter — something didn’t look right. And I told my wife, ‘That helicopter is not flying right.’”
Sevanesian said he saw the helicopter gradually losing altitude. Then, he said, he pulled over near the crash as fire roared.
“It was one of the most violent fires I had ever seen,” Sevanesian recalled.
He said he soon found a person down near the wreckage and three others “screaming uncontrollably.”
“It was very terrifying and sad for everyone,” Allyona said.
The Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement Wednesday that it would be involved in the investigation, which it said the National Transportation Safety Board would lead.

The NTSB said in a statement Wednesday that it was “investigating the Sept. 15 crash of a Eurocopter AS 350 B2 helicopter in Chatsworth, California.” It added that its investigators are expected to arrive on scene Wednesday morning.

Speaking near the scene Tuesday night, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said it was “a heartbreaking night for our city.” She praised first responders for their quick reaction and expressed grief over those who were killed in the bus collision and the aircraft crash.
“We lost five Angelenos today,” she said, “and my heart certainly goes out to the family and friends of all of those that we lost.”
California Gov. Gavin Newsom also thanked first responders and offered condolences in a statement on X.
“Our hearts are with the victims and families of tonight’s devastating Metro bus and helicopter crashes in Chatsworth, and with the entire NBC4 family,” he said.

title: Talking Shop with Ciara Miller ahead of her ‘Dancing with the Stars’ debut
summary: Summer House star Ciara Miller is competing on Dancing with the Stars season 35. These are her rehearsal, recovery and performance essentials from Nexxus, Bala and more.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

She took the Hamptons by storm from the moment she joined the cast of Bravo’s Summer House. She held down the fort in Fiji while hosting Love Island: Aftersun. She modeled in campaigns for some of the biggest brands in the world. And now, Ciara Miller is tackling a new challenge: competing for the Mirrorball Trophy on season 35 of Dancing with the Stars, which premiers tonight at 8 p.m. ET on ABC/Disney+.

“I’m definitely getting a run for my money,” says Miller, who told me that she’s wanted to do the show for years. “It’s such an experience for growth. I danced growing up, but I did ballet and hip hop and jazz and stuff. This is such a different sector of dance that I wanted to experience.”

Miller’s partner this season is Brandon Armstrong, a multi-season DWTS pro. She says he’s been a great teacher and choreographer, but she’s putting her mark on performances, too. “Brandon is in charge of one thing: the dancing,” says Miller. “I’m in charge of everything else. We have creative calls where we can be as involved or not involved as we want, and I’m involved, even down to his outfits.”

Before Miller’s first live performance, I talked to her about what she’s using to recover after hours-long rehearsals and products she swears by on the dance floor. And, of course, because she’s the first Summer House cast member to be in the ballroom, I had to ask: If she could cast any of her other housemates on Dancing with the Stars, who would it be? “Kyle [Cooke] would be number one on my Mount Rushmore,” says Miller. “I tried to teach him a pose, and I would really enjoy seeing Kyle attempting to learn any type of dance at all.”
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Bala Bangles Wrist & Ankle Weights

One of the most useful purchases Miller has made during Dancing with the Stars rehearsals so far is Bala Bangles. “I just got these arm weights because a lot of my moves this first week are in frame, and my arms look like chicken wings instead of an elegant bird,” she says. “So I was like, okay, what can keep me mindful of keeping my arms up? These weights are how I’ve been training my arms.” She got a pink pair and tries to keep them on for the entirety of each practice session.
Dr. Teal’s Pure Epsom Salt Sooth & Sleep with Lavender

Miller isn’t shy about sharing what the hardest part about being on Dancing with the Stars is: “I am not flexible anymore, so I really have to stretch,” she says. “My back, my neck… I’m so sore everywhere.” She’s taking recovery very seriously, starting with hot baths. “I’m soaking in a bathtub almost every day for at least 20 minutes. It’s essential,” says Miller. “I’m living for Dr. Teal’s epsom salt. I’ve got the sleepytime one, I’ve got the one for muscle recovery; I’ve got all the things.”
Currentbody LED Red Light Therapy Face Mask

To continue winding down after her bath, Miller puts on her favorite red light therapy mask from Currentbody. “It’s flexible, so it can fit into small spaces, and I didn’t have to worry about crushing it when I was traveling, which was nice,” she says, referring to her recent move from New York City to Los Angeles. “I use it to relax and treat my skin, and I’m incorporating getting massages, too, because I need to get better about recouping. But at home, it’s the simple things. I obviously love my bed, and I love a Salt & Stone candle — it’s one of my favorite things to have in my room.”
Homedics Bubble Mate Foot Spa

Miller isn’t just dancing for hours a day — she’s doing so while wearing heels. “You’ve got to break your shoes in and get used to them,” she says. “I’ve honestly been doing good so far and wearing socks with them. I’m the type of person where wearing a new shoe sometimes almost stresses me out, unless it’s for the look. But in this case, I knew I had to get acquainted with them early.”

One of her go-to ways to care for achy feet is by using a foot spa. “I’m bringing back the pedicure bath things that I was like, I haven’t seen this thing in 20 years,” she says. “But I got one on Amazon, and I would say it’s one of my best purchases of 2026.”
Solely Organic Mango Fruit Jerky

As for Miller’s favorite thing to nosh on pre-, post- and during rehearsal? “Fruit — I don’t like eating a heavy meal beforehand,” she says. “I love Solely fruit jerky. I swear by it and it helps spike my blood sugar if I’m feeling a little bit eh. It’s healthy and really great on the go.” There’s always Celcius in her refrigerator too, a brand she recently worked with to launch its Spritz Vibe beverage.
Nexxus Air Shape Workable Hold Texture Spray

Miller immediately stocked her DWTS trailer with Nexxus hair care when she got access to it. She’s been working with the brand throughout the year, and says its products continuously fit into different aspects of her life.

“With Dancing with the Stars, we’re going to be in several different types of hairstyles, so you really need something that’s going to withstand the test of time from the wee hours of the morning to at night when we’re live on TV,” says Miller. “We all know I’m a glam girl — I love my glam, and obviously I’m going to be focused on it. But when it comes down to it, I need reliable products that I know are going to hold me through so my attention is on my dancing entirely.”

Her favorite Nexxus product is the Air Shape Workable Hold Texture Spray. “I like volume. I like big hair. I want to pull it out and make it even bigger,” says Miller. “I’m a texture girl. And obviously I need a firm hairspray to hold it all in place, too.”

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who writes our Talking Shop series, interviewing people like Paris Hilton, Maureen Kelly, Lindsay Hubbard and Chase Crawford. title: Here’s how to pick a Kindle that actually fits how you read (and your budget)
summary: We’ve used Amazon Kindles for more than a decade. Here’s everything you need to know about each model, and which one is right for you.
story: Amazon Kindle has been one of our favorite e-readers for years — some of our editors have actually been using them as far back as 2012. (The first Kindle came out in 2007). If you’re unfamiliar, they’re known for being lightweight, simple to use and make reading while on the go a lot more pleasant than using your phone or a tablet that wasn’t made for reading.

Now, nearly 20 years after the release of its first model, Amazon has a few versions, each with slight variations that can make it confusing to know which one is right for you, especially when most of them look the same at a glance. I’ve tested different Kindle devices for years, and explain the key differences below so you don’t spend your money only to find that you prefer a different option. Here’s how to pick the best Kindle for your needs.

Which is the best Kindle model to buy?

There are a handful of different Amazon Kindle models to choose from and which one will be best for you depends on your needs and the features you value. NBC Selected editors have tested nearly all of them, and they each have key differences that help you decide which one to buy.
Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024)

Adjustable light hue

The Kindle Paperwhite is the go-to model for many NBC Selected staffers, myself included. Like all Kindles, it has a glare-free screen that makes it easy to read outside, even under bright sunlight. What makes the Paperwhite our favorite is its long battery life (the longest of any Kindle) and adjustable hue — you can change the tone of the screen light to be warmer or cooler. The warmer hue in particular makes it easier on the eyes when reading in dark rooms.
I pair mine with a Kindle Paperwhite fabric case — it’s soft and slim, and automatically turns the screen off when closed.
Amazon Kindle (2024)
Compact and lightweightCompetitive price
Compact and lightweight

Less adjustable screenNot waterproof
Less adjustable screen

The plain Amazon Kindle, no tagline, is the model to get if you want the lowest-priced option. Despite its lower cost, using it is more or less a similar experience as any other Kindle — it uses the same software and same Kindle bookstore. Reading books and listening to audiobooks feels very similar on this (and every) Kindle.

It’s also the smallest and lightest Kindle at well under a half pound — the weight of an average-size orange. It doesn’t have the Paperwhite’s adjustable light hue and it isn’t waterproof so if you like to read at the beach or pool this may not be the one for you, but while you’re otherwise reading and swiping through your favorite book, you might not notice much of a difference.

Amazon’s first color e-reader, the Kindle Colorsoft is a great fit for anyone reading a lot of colorful comic books and graphic novels. It also makes highlighted text more noticeable and useful than on black and white Kindles.
Outside of the color screen, the Kindle Colorsoft is most similar to the Kindle Paperwhite: It has the same adjustable light hue, waterproof design and seven-inch screen size.

It isn’t the best option if you plan on mostly reading regular, black and white books — the screen has slightly less contrast, so black and white text looks a little less crisp than on the Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite.

If you want a Kindle that can also be your notetaking companion, the Kindle Scribe is what you’re looking for. Former NBC Selected production coordinator Kelsey Fredricks tested it for two months and loved how responsive the screen was for taking notes. It comes with a stylus that’s smooth, comfortable to use and attaches to the side of the device with magnets for convenient storage.
You can sort your notes and documents on the e-reader and send them to your phone, computer, email or printer easily, says Fredricks.

The Scribe is larger than other Kindles, which makes it more comfortable for note taking but a bit bulkier in your hands and bag. At nearly a pound, it’s also a much heavier model. This model has an LED screen that allows you to read in a dark room, though there is a version without the light, too. You can read more in our Amazon Kindle Scribe review.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Is it worth it to buy a Kindle in 2026?

An Amazon Kindle is a book-sized device that uses an electronic-ink screen to display text, which simulates the appearance of ink on paper, says Nick Tanzi, assistant director of the South Huntington Public Library. E-ink screens are more comfortable to look at for long periods of time than smartphone or tablet screens, in our experience. They are also free of glare and reflections, which make them easy to read outside in the sun, unlike a smartphone or tablet. You can adjust the brightness of the screen, change from light mode to dark mode and, with some models, change the warmth or cool hue of the light.
E-ink screens also use significantly less battery power than other kinds of screens — it’s part of the reason Kindle devices can go so long without needing a recharge.

Amazon Kindle devices connect to Wi-Fi so you can browse the Amazon Kindle store, where you can purchase and download e-books and audiobooks. Your Kindle can also typically sync to public library apps like Libby, so your loans will appear on your Kindle too. So investing in a Kindle is worth it if you’re an avid reader and prefer to have all your titles in one device, giving you several options anytime you like.
Is it worth getting a Kindle for kids?

Aside from the Kindle Scribe, all of the Kindles above come in kid-versions: The Kindle Kids, Kindle Paperwhite Kids and Kindle Colorsoft Kids. They are the same device as the “adult” version, but come with no ads, a protective cover and six months of Amazon Kids+, the brand’s age three to 12-book subscription service. If your child likes to read or you want to encourage them to, a Kindle Kids device is a worthwhile investment.
What is the Kindle Signature Edition?

Amazon also makes pricier versions of its Kindle Paperwhite and a Kindle Colorsoft, called Signature Editions. The Signature Edition models have more internal storage (32GB, up from 16GB), automatically adjust the screen brightness when you are in a bright or dark space, come without ads on the lockscreen and support Qi wireless charging.

For most people, I don’t think the Signature Edition is worth the extra cost — I have never come close to running out of storage on a Kindle, and the device has such good battery life that wired charging has never been an inconvenience.
What’s the difference between a tablet and a Kindle?

A tablet is more phone than e-reader: it can run hundreds of apps, including streaming platforms and video games. A Kindle is optimized for reading, and can’t do nearly as much as a tablet on purpose. Devices like the Boox Palma 2 toe the line between phone, tablet and e-reader.
Frequently asked questions

It depends on the size and type of book. An average e-book file is around 2MB, in my experience, and most Kindles come with 16GB of internal storage: that means it can store thousands of e-books easily. Be aware that graphic novels, cookbooks and comic books take up significantly more storage space.

If you have an active Prime Membership, Prime Reading is free, and allows you to access several e-books, audiobooks, magazines, and comic books at no cost. You do still have to pay for your Kindle device separately, and not all titles you are looking for will be free. However, Amazon often offers deals on Kindle Unlimited during Amazon Prime Day, Prime Big Deal Days and other sales events.

You can use your public library card to borrow e-books, audiobooks and other material free of charge, just like going to the library in-person. I use and love the library app Libby, which makes it easy to sync borrowed e-books from my phone to my Kindle.
Meet our e-reader expert

At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest.

title: U.S. accuses Russia of plot to kill a prominent dissident in Washington
summary: The Kremlin orchestrated a murder-for-hire plot against a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C., this summer, the Department of Justice has said, as it unsealed charges against five people it alleged were part of a “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem around the world.”
story: The Kremlin orchestrated a murder-for-hire plot against a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C., this summer, the Department of Justice has said, as it unsealed charges against five people it alleged were part of a “global assassination network” aimed at causing “destruction and mayhem around the world.”

The five people charged are still at large, the DOJ said in the indictment unsealed late Tuesday, describing the wider operation being run by Russian intelligence as “brazen, aggressive, and far-reaching.”
The FBI said it had disrupted the plot, although officials did not detail how.

Since at least 2024, the network is alleged to have paid Americans and foreigners to spy on targets, “carry out targeted killings,” and “commit acts of terrorism against civilian and military infrastructure in European countries that are aligned, or perceived to be aligned, with Ukraine,” the DOJ said.

Asked for a response to the allegations by NBC News, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a daily briefing call with reporters that “until we have heard or seen any reasonable evidence and arguments based on at least something tangible, we do not consider it necessary to comment on this news.”
Russia has for decades been accused by Western governments of carrying out attempted and successful killings abroad. Despite substantial evidence, it has always denied these allegations.

The indictment did not name the intended victim in Washington. The DOJ lists the defendants as Yuri Khrameev, known as “Colonel Yuri,” 63, and his son Kirill Khrameev, 27, both of Russia; Oemis Romagoza Durruthy and Yaidel Delgado Suarez, known as “Viking,” both 35 and Cuban nationals; and Angel Eduardo Castro, 22, of Venezuela.
The indictment describes Durruthy as “an influential member of the Cuban diaspora living in Russia,” where it says Suarez and Castro also reside.
All face a conspiracy to finance terrorism charge. Yuri Khrameev, Suarez and Castro face an additional charge of conspiracy to commit murder for hire.
Yuri Khrameev is alleged to be a former Russian intelligence colonel, while his son is an officer in Russia’s Federal Security Service, or FSB.

Prosecutors allege the network recruited a Venezuelan citizen living in Brooklyn this summer, promising him between $1,000 and $1,500 to photograph and film two locations associated with the Washington target.

The man carried out the surveillance but declined an offer from Suarez and Castro of $40,000 to “eliminate” or “disappear” the target himself, prosecutors said. The alleged recruiters asked whether he knew somebody who would.
Suarez also offered substantial sums of money to other people in the U.S. to finish the job, the indictment said.

Messages quoted in the indictment show the conspirators allegedly referring to murder as “construction.” Surveillance instructions included putting the man’s phone into airplane mode and filming while passing the house.
Suarez allegedly said he also had people in Mexico who could carry out the killing, but they were delayed.
A second alleged plot involved a dissident believed to be living in Lithuania who the network accused of making derogatory statements about Russia.

In that case, a U.S. citizen was promised $200 to photograph the target’s address in 2025, then offered around $25,000 to kill him, prosecutors said. When he refused, Yuri Khrameev allegedly offered a “simpler job” — setting fire to a warehouse or attacking an electricity substation.
The purpose, Khrameev allegedly said, was to target “all the countries that are helping Ukraine.”
Durruthy, meanwhile, is accused of coordinating logistics for attacks in Prague in June 2024 and Lithuania that September.
Lithuanian authorities had publicly named Durruthy as wanted in January in a case involving attempts to burn military equipment intended for Ukraine, according to Lithuanian broadcaster LRT.

“These defendants allegedly operated as part of a global assassination network that reached into the United States, attempting to recruit U.S. citizens and foreigners to carry out killings at the behest of the Kremlin,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg.
“Actions like these represent a gross violation of our sovereignty and a threat to our national security.”
James C. Barnacle Jr., head of New York’s FBI office, said the agency “disrupted this operation through relentless work and rock-solid partnership.”

title: House panel votes to hold Epstein associate Leon Black in contempt
summary: The move came after the House Oversight Committee accused the former Wall Street private equity investor of ignoring subpoenas in its probe of Jeffrey Epstein.
story: The House Oversight Committee voted Tuesday to recommend the full House find billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress over his refusal to comply with subpoenas related to its probe into the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
The bipartisan vote was unanimous, 41-0.

Black, a private equity investor who had a business relationship with Epstein, voluntarily sat for a closed-door transcribed interview with the Republican-led committee in late June but left before it was over, after lawmakers complained he wasn’t answering their questions. As a result, they issued subpoenas for him to turn over more information.
He didn’t show up for a later deposition the committee scheduled and sued it, seeking to block the subpoenas for his appearance and nondisclosure agreements tied to Epstein.
Attorneys for Black called the committee’s action a “complete abomination” in a statement ahead of the vote called by Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., the committee chair.

“This is retaliation — plain and simple,” the attorneys, Susan Estrich and Aaron Cutler, wrote. “We have the constitutional right to sue Chairman Comer and the Committee because the subpoenas issued were illegitimate, illegal and a textbook abuse of power designed to bully and destroy legal protections of private citizens.”
Black is a co-founder and former head of Apollo Global Management, one of Wall Street’s most prominent investment firms.

He announced he was stepping down as CEO in January 2021 after an internal review found he had paid Epstein $158 million for advice on tax and estate planning and related services from 2012 to 2017. The review found that Black wasn’t involved in Epstein’s criminal activities.

Black has said he didn’t engage in any wrongdoing and “deeply” regrets his involvement with Epstein, who died in jail in 2019 awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges. Black hasn’t been accused of wrongdoing by law enforcement, and he has denied any involvement in or awareness of Epstein’s illegal activity.
After the Oversight contempt recommendation, the next step would be for the House to vote on the resolution. But it’s not a guarantee.
Comer told NBC News after Tuesday’s vote that he expects the House to take up the resolution on Thursday.
Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the committee, said “today’s a really important day for justice.”
He add that the committee will “work towards a strong vote of the House in a bipartisan way to get and ensure that we get our testimony and that Leon Black faces justice for these two subpoenas.”

title: Kash Patel defends FBI’s new policy on bestiality at Senate hearing
summary: Sen. John Kennedy grilled the FBI director about a recently revised policy that doesn’t automatically disqualify job applicants who have engaged in bestiality.
story: FBI Director Kash Patel on Tuesday found himself defending a new policy at the bureau that does not immediately disqualify potential hires who have engaged in bestiality.

At a Senate Judiciary Committee oversight hearing, some senators grilled Patel about the new standards, which he said were established so as not to discriminate against potential victims of sex trafficking who were forced to perform acts of bestiality.
His explanation elicited curious responses, including one from Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., who asked Patel why he would “even get into bestiality.”
Patel quickly emphasized that “we’re not into bestiality,” to which Kennedy said, “I know you’re not,” prompting a chuckle from Patel, who said he was trying to explain the policy.
Kennedy asked, “If Joe participated in bestiality, not as animal but as the human, don’t you think he ought to be disqualified?”
“If he voluntarily did it, sure. But if he was trafficked into it ...,” Patel responded.

Kennedy went on to ask how a person would “involuntarily do it.” Patel said human traffickers forced people into types of conduct like bestiality and “degrading acts of all kinds” in “a lot of cases.”

He said people at the bureau who suggested the policy change “explained to me and showed me cases in which people were forced into it and had applied to the FBI, and so I thought they should be considered. It’s not an automatic disqualification.”

Patel said that the previous policy addressed prostitution, trafficking and bestiality and that for bestiality, the rules “automatically disqualified any individual who participated on either side of it.”
“Either side of what? The bestiality?” Kennedy asked. “So you disqualified the animal?”
“Well, I don’t think — we have great canines, but we’re not going to disqualify them,” Patel said.
Add to Google
Add to Google
Sen. Dick Durbin, D-Ill., also inquired about the policy change, asking Patel whether he believed applicants who had engaged in bestiality were qualified candidates whom the FBI was losing.

“Applicants who have engaged in bestiality means they were victims of bestiality because they were forced to do so. And at this FBI, we are not going to criminalize and prevent victims from serving the United States of America and the premier law enforcement agency in the world,” Patel responded, adding he had “eliminated the bureaucracy that prevented these great Americans from serving, or at least being considered to serve.”

The oftentimes tense hearing included Democrats’ pressing Patel on broader topics about his leadership at the bureau and grilling him about his suit against a reporter for The Atlantic and firings and departures at the FBI since he took over.
While Patel was mostly praised by Republicans in the room, he drew heat from Kennedy over the change in hiring practices.
“You’re not telling us today that if a human being had sex with an animal that they can still be an FBI agent, are you?” Kennedy asked. “They can’t be, can they?”
“They cannot,” Patel responded.
“In fact, they ought to be in jail, right?” Kennedy said.
“They all are,” Patel said.

title: ‘I’m not going to be a Republican!’: John Fetterman promises, again, not to defect
summary: The Pennsylvania senator, who has faced ongoing questions about leaving the Democratic Party, appeared by video at the Republicans’ midterm convention last week.
story: WASHINGTON — Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., insisted Tuesday he won’t become a Republican, showing frustration with the ongoing questions about his intentions.
Sen. Fetterman says he won't switch to Republican Party
“I’m not going to be a Republican!” Fetterman said to reporters on Capitol Hill, raising his voice and shaking his head. “If I turn a Republican, then I’ll be a liar.”

“My name is not on the ballot. Like, chill and wait for the midterm here,” he added. “I’ve always been a Democrat. It’s like, no matter how many times I say that, I’m still getting asked just getting into the elevator.”

Fetterman, first elected in 2022, has grown increasingly distant from his party, mainly over his impassioned and unyielding defense of Israel and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He’s a regular guest on Fox News, where he gets asked about left-wing members of the Democratic Party and readily whacks them.
Those positions and actions have drawn significant attention on Fetterman as a Democrat but would become far less remarkable if he defected to the GOP.

Fetterman sparked the speculation in mid-July when he opened the door to leaving the Democratic Party if it “officially” became “anti-Israel” in the party platform. As Republicans invited him to defect, he wondered aloud to NBC News days later whether Democrats still want him in the party. In response, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., called Fetterman “a very good member of Congress” and one Democrats respect.

The speculation arose again last week when Fetterman made a video appearance at the two-day Republican midterm convention in Dallas to introduce his “friend” Sen. David McCormick, R-Pa. Fetterman issued a statement shortly after that saying he won’t switch parties if Democrats capture Senate control in November.

His seat comes up for re-election in 2028, and Fetterman’s prospects of winning renomination as a Democrat are rapidly fading. A New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll last month found Fetterman’s approval rating among Democrats was just 22%, having fallen precipitously from 74% in May 2024.

Yet, despite his rising approval rating among Pennsylvania Republicans in the same poll, his prospects of winning a GOP primary may be even more remote. Fetterman would have to defend his wide array of liberal positions — on matters such as expanding healthcare access, raising the federal minimum wage, supporting LGBTQ rights and championing legal abortion.

On Tuesday, Fetterman ignored questions about a recently created X account reportedly run by his former staffers who have turned against him. He also declined to comment on a recent Wall Street Journal report detailing examples of Fetterman showing a lack of interest in doing the job of a senator, citing interviews with more than a dozen former staffers and lawmakers. Neither he nor his office commented for that story, but Fetterman called its reporting “smears” in a statement to CNN.
One person who was quick to defend Fetterman was McCormick.

“These stories are the latest example of outrageously disloyal staff and forces on the Left using anonymous leaks to cancel my friend John Fetterman,” he said on X. “They hate that he is an independent thinker who refuses to fall into line so they want to silence him.”
